# Specification quality audit 008: Claude Fable report

[Audit directory format](../README.md) · [Navigation](README.md)

Claude Fable 5.2 assessed commit `e88d0c6cb` on 2026-11-24, orchestrating
Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents, each given an explicit model and
effort. The owner asked for a full audit of the specifications: incoherences,
errors and problems; legibility, objectivity and redundancy; fitness as the
input of AI coding agents, for the best and safest code; and a plan to
optimize them.

Scope: every page under `specs/`, 63 pages and 5.34 MB, read in full by lanes
with fixed line ranges; the code, the tests, the skills and the earlier
audits as evidence. The report records 1,574 verified findings
(33 High, 655 Medium, 886 Low; none Blocking), 51
candidates that verification refuted, a measured baseline, a plan in four
lanes and seventeen decisions that only the owner can take. It changes no
product code, contract, specification or milestone state, and authorizes no
implementation or live run.

## How to read it

- [Section 1](#1-the-request-and-the-verdict): the verdict, the scorecard and
  the seven actions that matter most.
- [Section 7](#7-the-plan): the plan, its order, its targets, and in
  [7.11](#711-decisions-only-the-owner-can-take) the owner's decisions.
- [Section 2](#2-measured-baseline): the numbers behind both.
- [Sections 3 to 6](#3-incoherences-and-errors): one class of finding each,
  with the examples that matter.
- [Section 10](#10-findings-catalog): any one finding.
  [10.2](#102-index-of-high-findings) lists the High findings.
- [Section 8](#8-method-and-limits): how the audit worked and what it cannot
  claim. [Section 9](#9-earlier-audits): what became of audit 004.

## 1. The request and the verdict

### 1.1 The request

The owner asked, on 2026-11-24:

> perform a full audit on specs, searching for incoherences, error, problems
>
> check for improvements in term of legibility, objectivity, removing
> redundancies, optimized for vibe coding and to create the best and safest
> code
>
> then propose a plan to optimize specs

The audit reads this as three questions and one deliverable:

1. Where are the specifications incoherent or wrong?
2. Where can they be more legible and more objective, and what do they repeat?
3. Are they the best input for the AI agents that write the code, so that the
   code is correct and safe?
4. A plan to optimize them.

"Specs" is every page under `specs/`: the normative pages, the deferred
designs and the milestone pages. Code, tests, skills, knowledge pages and
operator documentation were read as evidence.

### 1.2 The verdict

**The specifications are precise and safety-minded, and they have grown
faster than the process that keeps them correct.** Nothing in the findings asks for a change of
direction. No finding is Blocking. 33 are High, 655 Medium and
886 Low, in 1,574 findings that stand after verification
(1,263 defects of the text and 311 patterns of form).

What is right, and should stay:

- **The rules fail closed, and most say how.** Of 1,672 rules that cause or
  guard an effect, about three in four state the proof they need, and about three in four
  state what happens on failure ([section 2.9](#29-effect-rules-proof-failure-and-test)).
- **A column that a test compares with the code stays equal to the code.**
  Thirty inventories are held by a listed test. The drift was found in the
  tables that no test holds, and in the columns that a test leaves out ([section 2.8](#28-inventories-and-the-tests-that-hold-them)).
- **The `Not yet met` form works where it is used.** All 52 paragraphs name
  an item that is still open; none names delivered work
  ([section 2.6](#26-references-inside-rules)). Audit 004 had found 12 of
  53 stale, mis-owned or unchecked.
- **Decisions do not hide rules.** Of 25 sampled decisions that no page
  cites, none holds a binding rule that the specs lack
  ([Appendix B](#appendix-b-working-tables-of-the-cross-cutting-lanes), lane
  X7).
- **The API reference pages are written as rules.** `api/machines.md` and
  `api/environment.md` are among the pages with the shortest sentences and
  with the most sampled sentences that a test can be derived from
  ([section 2.5](#25-sentence-form)).

What is wrong:

- **33 rules are unsafe, contradictory or missing on paths that
  matter.** In at least six the code already follows the wrong rule, and
  three of those are on secret or destructive paths: a held secret can be
  deleted and regenerated ([SEC-2](#sec-2)), a plain `http://`
  BMC counts as verified for a disk erase ([API-3](#api-3)), and a revealed
  secret can land in sudo's output log ([SEC-1](#sec-1)).
- **Text and code have drifted apart in both directions.** Safety behavior
  that only the code states: who may override a delegated session
  ([API-4](#api-4)), what proves that a host account is Bootwright's to
  delete ([API-2](#api-2)). Text the code does not follow: a filesystem
  creation command ([CEPH-3](#ceph-3)), a command that no longer exists
  inside a data-loss remedy ([CTX-1](#ctx-1)).
- **One fact is stated on several pages, in different words, and 18% of
  those facts have drifted** ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)). The corpus
  does not copy sentences; it paraphrases rules, which no tool can find.
- **The form hides the rules.** Half of the sampled sentences carry more
  than one rule. The longest sentence is 275 words and lists the whole
  content of a Kickstart file ([section 2.5](#25-sentence-form)).
- **An agent loads a lot and still guesses.** In twelve dry runs the median
  task loaded 76 KB, guessed six times and ended at a confidence of 3 out
  of 5 ([section 2.3](#23-what-a-coding-agent-loads-and-where-it-guesses)).
- **The corpus grows faster than anyone consolidates it**: 9.2 times in ten
  weeks, while the 24 oversized sections of four weeks ago are all still
  oversized, 259 items await acceptance and 33 decisions await review
  ([sections 2.1](#21-size-and-growth) and [2.11](#211-delivery-pages)).

### 1.3 How findings are rated

- **Blocking**: implemented as written, the text causes or permits loss of
  data, destruction of something Bootwright does not own, disclosure of
  secret material or privilege beyond the stated boundary; or two rules on
  such a path contradict, so an implementer must guess.
- **High**: a contradiction, error or gap that changes what an implementing
  agent builds or what an operator does on a lifecycle, access or recovery
  path; or a statement on a safety, security or operator-facing page that
  names something that no longer exists.
- **Medium**: text that misleads or forces a guess without changing a
  destructive or security outcome.
- **Low**: editorial.

A verifier rated each finding by these definitions, not by its finder's
claim ([section 8.3](#83-verification)). No finding stands at Blocking. The
two that come closest are [SEC-2](#sec-2) and [OCP-1](#ocp-1). In SEC-2 the
version that the effect rests on stays in custody; what an operator's own
`secret delete` loses is the copy that a command can show. In OCP-1 the
owner's decision D269 already says which rule holds, and the defect is the
page that was not brought in line. A refuter, a judge and a third reader
read each one and left it at High.

### 1.4 Scorecard

The first four rows are the orchestrator's judgment on the scale that audit
004 used: 5, sound with only Low defects; 4, defects that mislead a reader
but change no destructive or security outcome; 3, a sound core with defects
that change what an operator or an agent does; 2, a Blocking finding on a
destructive path; 1, the design must change. The other rows are the mean of
the 39 legibility lanes' scores, where 5 means an agent can implement from
the text in one pass, 3 means it works at the cost of re-reading or a hunt,
and 1 means an agent would get it wrong.

| Dimension | Score | Basis |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Coherence between and within pages | 3 | No Blocking finding. 134 of 752 shared facts drifted; 163 findings of two pages that disagree and 156 of a page that contradicts itself |
| Truth against the code | 3 | 82 findings of text the code does not follow and 76 of behavior no page states; 34 of 71 inventories have no test |
| Safety rules | 3 | 9 High findings on a proof, an authorization or a bound; about a quarter of effect rules leave the proof or the failure behavior unstated |
| Delivery pages | 3 | The identifiers and the scope rules hold; 259 items await acceptance; 16 unreviewed decisions are cited as the basis of rules |
| Findable | 3.3 | about 6 of 30 routing questions land on the owning section within budget, by one lane's count |
| Bounded | 2.7 | 96 level-2 sections above 8 KB; a median task loads 76 KB |
| Single source | 3.0 | about 212 KB restated outside the owning sections, by the sweeps' estimate |
| Unambiguous | 3.0 | 17 of 28 load-bearing terms used with two or more meanings |
| Testable | 3.5 | 38% of sampled sentences yield a test alone, 79% with their section |
| Current | 3.2 | 37 statements of availability outside the `Not yet met` form; removed command names in rules |
| Economical | 2.6 | 14% of sentences above 40 words; the lanes estimate that 9% to 22% of each normative page could go without losing a rule |

### 1.5 The seven actions that matter most

These are the audit's proposals, in the order of [section 7](#7-the-plan).

1. **Fix the three rules that the code follows wrongly**, each with a test
   that fails first: refuse `secret delete` under a hold ([SEC-2](#sec-2));
   require `https://` for a verified BMC wherever that predicate is used
   ([API-3](#api-3)); refuse a reveal when sudo logs output
   ([SEC-1](#sec-1)).
2. **Write down the safety rules that only the code knows**, after a security
   review that the code is right ([API-4](#api-4), [API-2](#api-2),
   [CEPH-4](#ceph-4), [SEC-4](#sec-4)), and record as open gaps the six
   that need the owner's choice.
3. **Close the contradictions on recovery paths**, where a wrong reading
   sends an operator to destroy a cluster or records a failure as certain
   ([ADD-2](#add-2), [REC-1](#rec-1), [CLI-3](#cli-3), [CLI-4](#cli-4)).
4. **Add the checks that stop these classes from returning**, beside the
   first fixes and not after them: the list of table-holding tests is
   complete; a command or a code named in a spec exists; a table that a
   test holds is also checked in the parts its test leaves out; availability
   is stated only as `Not yet met` ([section 7.5](#75-lane-k-checks)).
5. **Then the Medium findings on safety, failure and missing rules, page by
   page**, starting with the six that can harm what Bootwright does not own.
   The drifted copies become links when the owner extends the program
   ([section 7.4](#74-lane-c-content)).
6. **Make new text follow one writing standard now**, so that 164 KB a week
   stops adding to the backlog, and rewrite old text only after one measured
   pilot ([section 7.7](#77-lane-f-form-and-routing)).
7. **Give the owner one sitting of sixteen decisions**, with a seventeenth
   after the pilot, and review the 16 pending decisions that rules already
   rest on
   ([section 7.11](#711-decisions-only-the-owner-can-take)).

## 2. Measured baseline

This section holds numbers, not judgments. A figure marked "measured" was
computed by a script over the audited tree, and the script's rule is stated. A
figure marked "lane" is one lane's own count from its working table; working
tables were not verified ([section 8.5](#85-limits)).

### 2.1 Size and growth

Measured with `git ls-tree` at the last commit of each date.

| Date | Pages | Normative bytes | Deferred bytes | Milestone bytes | Total bytes | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-09-15 | 25 | 579,103 | 0 | 0 | 579,103 | |
| 2026-10-01 | 42 | 765,287 | 76,501 | 205,414 | 1,047,202 | +468,099 |
| 2026-10-15 | 48 | 1,143,287 | 69,174 | 808,949 | 2,021,410 | +974,208 |
| 2026-10-26 | 51 | 1,801,812 | 68,049 | 1,521,007 | 3,390,868 | +1,369,458 |
| 2026-11-01 | 51 | 2,011,533 | 54,236 | 1,804,081 | 3,869,850 | +478,982 |
| 2026-11-10 | 57 | 2,279,219 | 72,278 | 2,242,893 | 4,594,390 | +724,540 |
| 2026-11-17 | 61 | 2,420,167 | 72,214 | 2,524,652 | 5,017,033 | +422,643 |
| 2026-11-24 | 63 | 2,607,035 | 72,211 | 2,664,540 | 5,343,786 | +326,753 |

The corpus is 9.2 times its size of ten weeks ago. The normative pages grew
4.5 times, from 0.58 MB to 2.61 MB. In the last two weeks the normative pages
grew by about 164 KB a week and the milestone pages by about 211 KB a week.
At four bytes a token the normative pages are about 650,000 tokens and the
whole corpus about 1.3 million.

Since the previous audit's baseline (`931cfb596`, 2026-11-10), 684 commits
landed. Together they changed 53 spec pages: 19,286 lines added and 3,491
removed.

### 2.2 How an agent reaches a rule

Measured over `specs/index.md`, 79 links:

| Link target | Links | Of them above 24,576 bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| A whole page | 43 | 29 |
| A level-2 section | 19 | 3 |
| A level-3 section | 14 | 0 |
| Outside `specs/`, or a directory | 3 | |

The first routing table holds 43 links, and 40 of them name a whole page. The
29 whole-page links above the section budget name 4.25 MB between them. The
second table, "Sections of the largest domains", routes into six of the 28
normative pages above 24 KB.

Lane X1 traced 30 concrete questions of an implementing agent through
`AGENTS.md` and the index only:

| Where the route lands | Questions |
| --- | ---: |
| On the owning section, within budget | 6 |
| On the owning section, above budget | 2 |
| On the right page, with no section named (median load about 90 KB, against an owner of about 10 KB) | 17 |
| On the owner only through a link inside a routed section | 2 |
| On a page the index does not route, or on a rule with two owners | 3 |

These are the lane's summary counts. Its working table differs by one in the
first and in the last row, and a verifier could not reproduce the traces, so
the counts show a proportion and not exact figures.

Five normative pages have no row of their own in the index
(`cli/cluster-access.md`, `cli/cluster-admin-credentials.md`,
`managed-os-satellite.md`, `managed-os-subscription-source.md`,
`ceph-subscription-dependencies.md`); each is within two links of it, which is
all the reachability test asks. The sections other pages link to most, and
that the index does not name, are (links, source pages):
`substrates.md#kubevirt-machine-realization` (36, 14),
`state-reconciliation.md#lifecycle-unit` (34, 12),
`controller.md#the-controller-stage` (25, 12), `api.md#object-names` (24, 15),
`openshift-clusters.md#installation` (24, 11),
`state-reconciliation.md#produced-material-custody` (23, 13),
`ceph.md#frozen-release-and-trust` (23, 9),
`managed-os.md#automatic-root-disk-discovery` (23, 3) and
`infrastructure-services.md#host-reservations` (22, 10).

### 2.3 What a coding agent loads, and where it guesses

Twelve dry runs gave a Sonnet agent a realistic task and the repository's own
routing rule, and asked for an implementation brief, not an implementation
([section 8.2](#82-the-lanes)). Each run reported what it loaded, what it had
to guess and how confident it was (1 to 5) that an implementation from its
brief would be what the owner wants and safe.

| Task | Bytes loaded | Loads | Not needed in hindsight | Guesses | Confidence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Optional description on a Machine NIC | 54,122 | 18 | 15,697 | 6 | 3 |
| A stop of its own when a KubeVirt host cluster is unreachable at destroy | 78,600 | 17 | 17,134 | 6 | 2 |
| Continue, not reinstall, after a crash before the completion proof | 114,183 | 27 | 30,031 | 5 | 3 |
| `--timeout` on `machine exec` | 73,951 | 14 | 10,308 | 6 | 2 |
| A new managed infrastructure service kind | 155,000 | 23 | 12,500 | 9 | 2 |
| An unreachable OSD host during a Ceph destroy | 84,907 | 19 | 13,237 | 6 | 3 |
| A new built-in add-on package | 88,000 | 22 | 65,408 | 9 | 3 |
| `secret show` prints the last renewal | 62,000 | 14 | 2,000 | 6 | 2 |
| NVMe secure erase for data disks | 84,152 | 25 | 11,787 | 9 | 2 |
| An expiry date on a session grant | 65,100 | 18 | 14,040 | 9 | 3 |
| One more host package at install, removed at uninstall only if added | 66,330 | 14 | 20,343 | 6 | 4 |
| Refuse at plan when a root selector can match two disks | 52,055 | 11 | 12,236 | 5 | 3 |

The figures are the agents' own reports: in eight of the twelve runs the
total does not equal the sum of the loads the agent listed.
The median task loaded about 76 KB (19,000 tokens) in 18 loads, had to guess
six times and ended at confidence 3: five tasks at 2, six at 3 and one at 4. The previous
audit estimated 25,000 to 38,000 tokens for a task including the fixed
procedure files; these runs count spec and code reading only.

### 2.4 Units of loading: sections and budgets

Measured over the 46 normative pages with the rules of
`test/docs/docs_gates_test.go` (a level-2 section at most 24,576 bytes; a leaf,
a heading of level 3 or deeper up to the next heading, at most 8,192 bytes):

| Unit | Count | Median bytes | 90th percentile | Largest | Above 8,192 | Above 24,576 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Level-2 section | 379 | 3,334 | 17,177 | 87,580 | 96 | 7 |

## 3. Incoherences and errors

This section answers the first question of the request: where the specifications are incoherent or wrong. Each subsection takes one class of finding. The counts include the patterns of form that carry the same defect; [section 10](#10-findings-catalog) holds every finding.

| Class | Section | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Two pages state one rule differently | [3.1](#31-rules-that-two-pages-state-differently) | 7 | 104 | 52 | 163 |
| A page contradicts itself | [3.2](#32-pages-that-contradict-themselves) | 0 | 87 | 69 | 156 |
| A name that no longer exists; history as a rule | [3.3](#33-names-of-things-that-no-longer-exist-and-history-written-as-a-rule) | 2 | 83 | 69 | 154 |
| Text that the code does not follow | [3.4](#34-text-that-the-code-does-not-follow) | 5 | 41 | 36 | 82 |
| Binding behavior that no page states | [3.5](#35-binding-behavior-that-no-page-states) | 4 | 40 | 32 | 76 |
| **All** | | **18** | **355** | **258** | **631** |

### 3.1 Rules that two pages state differently

The audit found that the corpus seldom copies a sentence, but it often restates a rule in new words on a second page, and the second statement then drifts from its owner. Most drift is Medium: a reader must guess which page wins. Seven cases are High, and five of them sit on a recovery, removal or retry path, where the wrong reading changes what a destroy or a continuation does.

**The numbers.** The class holds 163 findings: 7 High, 104 Medium and 52 Low. 159 are single defects and 4 are patterns of form. 111 are new, 18 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, 4 are tracked by an open item, and 30 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. 37 were found by more than one lane. Over the whole corpus, a fact that two or more pages state has drifted on one of them in 134 of 752 cases ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)). The sweeps with the most drift are the CLI contract (12 of 47 facts), operations and locks (12 of 41), scope and lifecycle (12 of 45) and proxy, registries and trust (12 of 44).

| Area | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CLI | 0 | 17 | 13 | 30 |
| API | 0 | 12 | 11 | 23 |
| REC | 0 | 13 | 1 | 14 |
| CTX | 1 | 10 | 3 | 14 |
| CEPH | 1 | 8 | 4 | 13 |
| SEC | 1 | 8 | 3 | 12 |
| MIL | 0 | 9 | 2 | 11 |
| ARC | 2 | 5 | 2 | 9 |
| Other eight areas | 2 | 22 | 13 | 37 |

**What the defects look like.**

- The adapter protocol table in `architecture.md` drifted from the pages that own its parts. It says a lifecycle `prepared` record comes "only on an apply's own attempt" (`specs/architecture.md:1002`), but destroy attempts publish removal preparations through it, and the erase receipt and the Ceph cleanup receipt depend on that ([ARC-37](#arc-37)). The same section moves the controller run's `failed` versus `unknown` line to a different event than `controller.md` and the code ([ARC-1](#arc-1), `specs/architecture.md:1087`). An agent that builds from the table refuses a valid destroy record, or records `unknown` for a run that installed nothing.
- `security.md` restates the replay-safe removal retry and drops the owner's condition that the owning apply durably recorded an attempt ([SEC-3](#sec-3), `specs/security.md:42-46`). The restatement links its owner, but an agent that reads only this page allows a removal retry without proof of ownership.
- `add-ons.md` says another build continues an operation "only when re-planning yields the same request" (`specs/add-ons.md:202`). The continuation owner says continuation never requires the current planner to reproduce the saved requests ([ADD-1](#add-1)). Two more pages give a third and a fourth wording.
- `ceph-native-api.md` says the host request "never carries the member" `delegated` (`specs/ceph-native-api.md:270-272`), while the retained-root host inverse in `ceph.md` and the code use it ([CEPH-1](#ceph-1)).
- The OpenShift Replay paragraph says "a settled apply selects each node's disk again" (`specs/openshift-clusters.md:1040`), but a settled apply reaches no host ([OCP-2](#ocp-2)).
- The fresh-install remedies say the fresh install drops stored media (`specs/contexts/controller-record.md:122-124`), but uninstall refuses while the media store holds any image, so the operator meets a refusal the remedy did not mention ([CTX-2](#ctx-2)).
- Numbers and names copied into prose drift from the code. The plan bounds say "128 impacts and 8 resources" where the owner table and the code say 256 and 64 ([REC-16](#rec-16), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:972`). The setup-output retention rule is told in five places that disagree ([CTX-P3](#ctx-p3), `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:308`). The erase refusal list names 16 codes, and several differ from the stop codes in `cli/stops.md` with no stated mapping ([REC-P1](#rec-p1), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2926`). The SSH session row promises `255` for every refusal before the session opens and drops the usage and interrupt cases ([CLI-39](#cli-39), `specs/cli/output.md:23`).

**Why it happens.** A domain page restates an engine or architecture rule in its own words to make its own section readable. It links the owner, but no test holds the copy, so a later change to the owner does not reach it. [SEC-3](#sec-3) and [SUB-P4](#sub-p4) show restatements that link their owner and still lost a condition. Ownership is sometimes unclear: two pages each name the other as the owner of the operation log tree ([REC-7](#rec-7)), and the proxy grammar has two owners that defer to each other ([API-24](#api-24)). The repetition detector finds copies, not paraphrases, so this drift cannot be found by a tool ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)). The 18 findings that audit 004 already reported show that a restatement found once is not removed.

**What is right and should stay.** Most restatements still agree: 618 of the 752 facts compared match their owner ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)). Where a bound is held as a table row that names its Go constant, as the setup-output row at `specs/contexts.md:623` names `maxSetupRuns`, the number has one owner that the code holds ([CTX-P3](#ctx-p3)).

**What fixes the class.** Each rule needs one owning section, and other pages need a link to its anchor instead of a second wording. A number or a code name belongs in a table held by the code or a test, not in prose. The seven High contradictions need the owner reading chosen and the other page corrected first. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) gives the order and the details.

### 3.2 Pages that contradict themselves

None of the findings of this class is High. The audit found many pages that say two things about one case: a general rule says "only", "every", "never" or "the one exception", and a later passage on the same page adds a case that the general rule does not admit. In most of these findings the code follows one reading, so the defect lives in the text. It still forces a guess on every agent that reads the page.

The class holds 156 findings: 87 Medium, 69 Low, none High. Of them, 146 are single defects and 10 are patterns of form. 93 are new, 22 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, and 41 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. 29 were found by more than one lane.

| Area | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CEPH | 17 | 14 | 31 |
| CLI | 15 | 15 | 30 |
| API | 8 | 11 | 19 |
| REC | 10 | 4 | 14 |
| MOS | 7 | 3 | 10 |
| Other nine areas | 30 | 22 | 52 |

**A general rule and its exception, on one page.** The heaviest case is on a data path. `specs/ceph.md` says "nothing here clears a disk" and that a zap needs its own authorization, and the same section defines an owned clear that runs `ceph-volume lvm zap --destroy` during apply ([CEPH-59](#ceph-59), `specs/ceph.md:1365-1366`). An agent can remove the clear, or widen it. In the same way, destroy "retains evidence until positive removal or positive absence is durable", but an abandoned removal publishes pristine evidence while its effects stay on the host. Diff then reads the left grant as taken back ([REC-30](#rec-30), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1972`). The entry power check demands every target Machine off, with no exception for the Machines that a removal must reach while they run ([REC-35](#rec-35), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2512-2516`). The attacker model refuses a sticky ancestor directory for the re-executed binary, and the privilege section exempts a root-owned one ([SEC-15](#sec-15), `specs/security.md:58-60`).

**States with no clear exit, and conditions that cannot hold.** Two rows of the Ceph interruption table both match a readiness timeout after the services call: one continues, the other refuses `partial-cluster` with no forward exit ([CEPH-52](#ceph-52), `specs/ceph.md:1097-1098`). The media-release gate requires Completion, and Completion requires the media already released ([OCP-37](#ocp-37), `specs/openshift-clusters.md:971-974`). The wait rules for a provided Machine's update, hostname and registration form cycles when read literally ([MOS-26](#mos-26), `specs/managed-os.md:2073`). After `firmware-setting-not-applied` the machine may be on, but the Recovery paragraph says it is left off, and the remedy leaves out the forced stop ([SUB-46](#sub-46), `specs/substrates.md:1532-1533`).

**Tables that break their own column definitions.** The stop catalog defines certainty in one row. It then gives `unproved` to one adapter that ends without proving its postcondition and `possible` to another adapter for the same event ([CLI-54](#cli-54), `specs/cli/stops.md:30`). On some rows the Recovery class promises a different first step than the Remedy text, so a caller that acts on `abandon-context` deletes a context that the Remedy only asked it to verify ([CLI-P2](#cli-p2), `specs/cli/stops.md:230`).

**Closed lists that miss a member.** The list of commands that read standard input leaves out `cluster rsh` ([CLI-8](#cli-8), `specs/cli.md:253-254`). The `--ssh-*` scope says "only" seven commands, then names `machine enroll` ([CLI-P12](#cli-p12), `specs/cli/commands.md:12-15`). The Replay section's "only differences it converges" omits the resumed update ([MOS-12](#mos-12), `specs/managed-os.md:650-653`).

The findings show one cause. A decision or a later feature adds a case, and the edit adds a new passage but leaves the older general sentence as it was: the owned clear came with D225 and abandonment with D283, and neither edit scoped the sentence that it contradicts. The same thing happens to closed lists. A word such as "only", "every" or "the one exception" makes a claim about the whole page, and nothing checks that claim when the page grows. A second cause is a rule stated twice on one page, where the copies drift. [MOS-P19](#mos-p19) finds the network evidence and bounds of Network convergence stated twice, and the copies already differ. This is the same restatement drift that [section 2.7](#27-repetition) measures across pages, here inside one page.

Two things are right and should stay. In most findings one side of the contradiction is correct and matches the code, so the fix is a clause or a link, not a new design. The stop catalog defines each Certainty value in one row (`specs/cli/stops.md:30`), so a test can check every row against that definition.

To fix the class, every edit that adds an exception also scopes the general sentence it breaks and links the exception from it. Each closed list either points at the inventory the code owns or is held by a named test, and each rule is stated once per page. The stop catalog needs a stated rule for choosing a certainty value. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the details.

### 3.3 Names of things that no longer exist, and history written as a rule

The audit found that the corpus often keeps the old name after a command, flag, stop code or field is removed. It also keeps delivery state and history inside present-tense rules. Most of these defects are Medium: they mislead and force a guess. Two are High because they send an operator to a command that does not exist on a host-trust path and on a data-loss path.

The class holds 154 findings: High 2, Medium 83, Low 69. Of them, 123 are single defects of the text and 31 are patterns of form reported with a count. 27 were already reported by audit 004 and are still present. 38 were found by more than one lane.

| Area | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CEPH | 0 | 23 | 3 | 26 |
| MIL | 0 | 9 | 15 | 24 |
| API | 0 | 7 | 10 | 17 |
| CLI | 1 | 4 | 6 | 11 |
| DEF | 0 | 6 | 5 | 11 |
| other 11 areas | 1 | 34 | 30 | 65 |

The defects that matter most fall into four groups.

**Removed commands and codes in operator text.** [CTX-1](#ctx-1) finds the removed `plan` command still presented as a command on some twenty lines of normative pages, by its lane's count; the catalog has no such command. The data-loss remedy tells the operator to copy `<digest bootwright plan prints>` (`specs/managed-os.md:920`), and the lock table lists `plan` as a reader (`specs/contexts.md:381`). [CLI-2](#cli-2) finds that the host-key safeguard cites a `--observe-host-keys` flag and a `preflight` command that the "complete public command tree" does not list (`specs/cli/commands.md:501`). In the same way, the `power.unproved` remedy names `bootwright machine status`, which does not exist ([CLI-139](#cli-139), `specs/cli/stops.md:214`). The `--until` refusals name `lifecycle.stage`, a code that left the stop registry and is now three separate codes ([REC-20](#rec-20), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1214`).

**Historical shapes written as rules.** The development policy forbids older readers and tailored refusals for a historical shape. The specs still name such shapes: an index "carrying `qualification`" with a remedy that names a build ([REC-6](#rec-6), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:446`), "the former `Environment.spec.trustedCAs`" ([API-45](#api-45), `specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:359`), a Proxy configuration defined as "the one an earlier request version wrote" ([SVC-7](#svc-7), `specs/infrastructure-services.md:761`), and version-move and retirement guidance ([GOV-8](#gov-8), `specs/managed-os.md:2343`). Open items repeat this: B434 asks for a move to a `-v6` request when the code holds only `-v1` ([MIL-8](#mil-8), `specs/milestones/backlog.md:862`).

**Rules that point at the wrong item or state a false fact.** The host-identity owner says relocation "waits on B103", but the rebind was split out and delivered ([CTX-34](#ctx-34), `specs/controller.md:1069`). An operator may choose `context delete --purge` instead of the delivered rebind. `specs/ceph.md:1123` says every adapter run is held to 6h0m0s, which has been false since X313 ([CEPH-53](#ceph-53)).

**Deferred and coverage pages that describe replaced mechanisms.** The scenario design still prescribes the union plan and an unbuilt `DeltaAdmitter`, which the delivered additive apply replaced ([DEF-8](#def-8), `specs/deferred/reconciliation-scenarios.md:168`). An agent that revives the next scenario would build a second, incompatible mechanism. `specs/ceph-coverage.md` writes run state such as "remain unrun" and "currently supplies" as rule text in ten places, and two of them call answered questions open ([CEPH-P8](#ceph-p8), `specs/ceph-coverage.md:567`).

The findings show the cause. A rename or a removal changes the owner section and the code, but not the other sentences that name the old thing. [CTX-1](#ctx-1) even finds the stale name in a code constant, `lifecycle.DigestPlaceholder`, so the spec and the code drift together. Delivery state is written into a rule when work lands. It is not moved to the `Not yet met` form or to the milestone: of 62 availability statements in normative pages, 37 state an unmet rule outside that form ([section 2.6](#26-references-inside-rules)). Of 477 lines with an id, a date or a word of history, 150 are rationale and 51 are delivery history ([section 2.6](#26-references-inside-rules)). The tests hold the catalog tables, but no test checks the command, flag and code names that prose mentions.

Two things are right and should stay. The `Not yet met` paragraphs themselves are current: none of the 52 names a delivered item ([section 2.6](#26-references-inside-rules)). Most uses of "no longer", "replaced" and "renamed" in normative pages describe runtime state, not history, so a sweep must not remove them.

The class needs two changes. First, every removed name must leave the corpus with its removal, and a test must check the command, flag and stop-code names in spec prose against the catalog and the code. Second, history and delivery state must move out of rules, into the decision, the milestone or the `Not yet met` form, and sentences about historical shapes must be deleted, not reworded. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the steps.

### 3.4 Text that the code does not follow

The audit found 82 places where a spec states one thing and the code does another. In most of them the code is right and the text is out of date: the code changed, or was built from a fact the spec never got, and nothing held the spec equal to it. The class is large but simple to repair. Most fixes are one sentence, or a pointer to the code owner in place of a hand-copied list.

All 82 findings are single defects of the text. None is a pattern of form. By severity: 5 High, 41 Medium, 36 Low. By status: 46 are new, 7 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, and 29 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. 14 were found by more than one lane.

| Area | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CLI | 0 | 6 | 8 | 14 |
| API | 0 | 6 | 5 | 11 |
| REC | 2 | 5 | 4 | 11 |
| MOS | 0 | 7 | 2 | 9 |
| CEPH | 2 | 2 | 3 | 7 |
| ARC | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| SVC | 0 | 4 | 1 | 5 |
| Other areas (SUB, DEF, SEC, ADD, MIL, CTX) | 1 | 9 | 9 | 19 |

These numbers sit beside a wider sample. The lens A lanes checked 336 claims against the code: 254 match, 78 do not, and 4 could not be found ([section 2.8](#28-inventories-and-the-tests-that-hold-them)). The lanes chose which claims to check, so that is not a rate for the corpus.

**What the defects look like.**

Two Ceph commands in the specs do not work, and the worker deliberately does something else. [CEPH-129](#ceph-129): `specs/ceph.md:785-789` gives `osd pool create .rgw.root 32 32 replicated <ruleName> --autoscale_mode on`. Ceph reads `<ruleName>` as an erasure-code profile. For a name that starts with a dot, it also creates nothing yet answers success unless `--yes-i-really-mean-it` is given. [CEPH-3](#ceph-3): `specs/ceph-resources.md:126-131` puts `allow_standby_replay` into `ceph fs new` and says no `fs set` follows. On 20.2.1 that pair aborts the MON leader, so the worker sets the flag with a later `fs set`. In both cases the code is right. An agent that "fixes" the worker from the spec breaks the cluster.

The text describes a privileged remote path more narrowly than the code runs it. [SUB-2](#sub-2): `specs/substrates.md:1207` says the capacity observation runs with "no shell", but when the lifecycle account needs sudo, the code wraps each probe in `sudo -n -u root -- /bin/sh -c`. [ARC-4](#arc-4) (`specs/architecture.md:172-176`) leaves the same path out of the direct SSH exception. [SEC-19](#sec-19) (`specs/security.md:273-276`) names only one exception to the no-shell rule, although Go-side SSH commands also reach a remote shell through a quoting function the spec does not name. Whether the wrapper of [SUB-2](#sub-2) stays is the owner's choice ([section 7.11](#711-decisions-only-the-owner-can-take), decision 8). Either way the spec must state the escalation, the wrapper and the quoting, so a reviewer can judge them.

A closed list in the spec is narrower than the code's list. [REC-74](#rec-74): `specs/state-reconciliation.md:855-857` and `:1508-1511` say a read-only execution admits only `observe`, a lend and one named revoke. The code also admits two `prepare_credentials` entrypoints, and `TestReadOnlyEntrypointsAreExplicit` holds them. The code is right. The spec should point at that set and not copy it.

A rule that decides a refusal cannot be read. [REC-2](#rec-2): the controller-dependency sentence at `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1129-1134` does not parse. It also names `controller.unsupported`, where the engine refuses with `plan.controller-order`. Here the code (`DependOnController`) is the reference for the rewrite.

The spec states a weaker input boundary than the code enforces. [API-38](#api-38): `specs/api/machines.md:1236` gives the `packages.install` grammar as a deny-list, while `packageSpecPattern` is a strict allow-list. The code is right. An agent working from the text could widen a Kickstart injection boundary.

Some remedies and bounds tell the operator the wrong thing. [CLI-55](#cli-55): `specs/cli/stops.md:486` tells the operator to "erase every selected Ceph disk", while the raisers say to declare erasure authority in `hardware.dataDisks`. [SUB-23](#sub-23) (known to audit 004): `specs/substrates.md:2027` bounds a Redfish insert at 39 minutes 20 seconds. The code and its test hold 46 minutes 20 seconds, because the spec leaves out the certificate import. In both, the code is right.

Decisions also drift from the code. [MIL-17](#mil-17): D200 (8) at `specs/milestones/backlog.md:6563` admits stretch pools "with exactly four OSD hosts". That reads as refusing the six-OSD-host reference profile, which the code admits.

**Why it happens.** Most of these defects are hand-copied inventories with no test that compares them to the code. Examples are the read-only list ([REC-74](#rec-74)), the 17 Ceph refusal tokens at `specs/ceph.md:1227-1234` ([CEPH-56](#ceph-56)), the Redfish bounds ([SUB-23](#sub-23)) and the reference-edge rows ([REC-17](#rec-17), [MOS-83](#mos-83), [SVC-26](#svc-26)). This goes against convention C6. Where a test exists, it checks less than the table states. `TestEveryRequirementMatchesTheEdgeCatalog` only sees families that some example plans, and the Redfish bounds test compares constants with literals, never with the spec text. Native Ceph facts reached the worker and the knowledge page, but not the owning spec ([CEPH-129](#ceph-129), [CEPH-3](#ceph-3)). And lines changed after audit 004 had no review ([REC-2](#rec-2)).

**What is right and should stay.** The code side already owns most of these inventories, and often a test holds them, for example `TestReadOnlyEntrypointsAreExplicit`. Pointing at them is cheap. Also, many fixes are local: for [MOS-11](#mos-11), a grep found only the two places that write `context update` as a field name.

**What fixes the class.** Where the code owns an inventory, the spec names the Go symbol and the test, and it drops the copy. Where a table must stay, a docs check holds every column of it equal to the code. For each High finding, the text is corrected to the side this section names, before an agent builds from it. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the details.

### 3.5 Binding behavior that no page states

The audit found many rules that the product enforces but no spec states. The code, a decision, a milestone item or a delivered record holds the rule, and the owning spec page holds a principle, a gesture or nothing. The worst cases are on privilege, custody and destructive paths. There, an agent who works from the spec alone builds a weaker or a different control.

The class holds 76 findings: 4 High, 40 Medium and 32 Low. Of them, 74 are single defects and 2 are patterns of form reported with a count. 54 are new, 8 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, 1 is tracked, and 13 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. Seven were found by more than one lane.

| Area | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MIL | 0 | 9 | 9 | 18 |
| API | 1 | 9 | 5 | 15 |
| CEPH | 2 | 4 | 4 | 10 |
| CLI | 1 | 3 | 4 | 8 |
| MOS | 0 | 5 | 2 | 7 |
| Other ten areas | 0 | 10 | 8 | 18 |

The defects look like this:

- **Privilege boundaries held only in code.** [API-4](#api-4) (High): the delegated session page says a session "needs the configured remote account, key authentication and pre-established host trust" (`specs/api/session-access-policy.md:102`). It never states that the root entry refuses `--ssh-user`, `--ssh-id-file` and `--ssh-ask-password`, or that it turns off the escape character and all forwarding. The code does this in `internal/machine/sshlocal/argv.go:64`. In the same way, [MIL-197](#mil-197) shows that the sudo-entry guard admits "any variable outside what sudo sets" (`specs/security.md:469`), while the code holds a fixed list that no spec names.
- **A destructive admission with no list of stops.** [CLI-3](#cli-3) (High) and [CLI-P14](#cli-p14) share one cause. `specs/cli/stops.md:20` says a stop may attest that a failed removal is confined to its target, and `destroy --keep-going` relies on that. No row says which stops attest. In code, three do. The catalog test compares eight cells per row and never this field.
- **Ceph daemons with no admission rule.** [CEPH-2](#ceph-2) (High) and [CEPH-13](#ceph-13) show that the `delegated` listing in `specs/ceph-native-api.md:285` names no rule for `nvmeof`, `mgmt-gateway`, `oauth2-proxy` or SMB services. The code lists them. If an agent follows the spec, it either refuses valid clusters or admits these daemons without the host-set check.
- **Custody of a secret after a lost reply.** [CEPH-4](#ceph-4) (High): CephClient creation names "collision and ownership checks" (`specs/ceph-resources.md:593`), but no page defines the attempt record or the `foreign-client` refusal that the code has. One reading leaves the apply stuck. The other puts a foreign key into Bootwright custody.
- **Rules that live only in delivery pages.** [MIL-21](#mil-21): two `make release` refusals exist only in D251 (`specs/milestones/backlog.md:8649`). [MIL-52](#mil-52): the OVN reserved-name list sits in B718 (`specs/milestones/m3.md:1120`), and it has already drifted from the code, which also refuses `lo`. [MIL-25](#mil-25): "control-free" is defined only by the X102 record (`specs/milestones/delivered.md:6979`). When a delivery page closes or moves, these rules lose their only text.
- **Refusals without a code or a table row.** [ADD-P13](#add-p13) counts pre-contact refusals in `specs/add-ons.md` that are stated in prose with no code. The refusal table also reads as if it were complete. [CEPH-50](#ceph-50): the three-host floor and its refusal `ceph.unsupported-topology` have no spec row, and `specs/ceph.md:990` says only that fewer hosts "keep their existing refusal".
- **"Optional" that blocks every apply.** [API-142](#api-142): `capacityReserve` is called optional (`specs/api/machines.md:162`). But when it is omitted, capacity is unknown, and capacity admission then refuses every apply that starts a libvirt Machine.

The findings show why this happens. The code was written to close a gap that the spec left open, and the result was recorded in a delivered record or an item section, not in the owning spec. MIL is the largest area, and its findings name records such as X102, X326 and X372 as the only text of a rule. The tests do not catch the gap because they compare only some columns, as [CLI-P14](#cli-p14) shows and [section 2.8](#28-inventories-and-the-tests-that-hold-them) measures: 34 of 71 inventories are held by no test, and the held refusal tables leave a column unchecked. Only 11% of effect rules name the test that holds them ([section 2.9](#29-effect-rules-proof-failure-and-test)). So nothing forces the spec to follow the code.

Some things are right and should stay. The code enforces these rules, and in several findings, for example [API-4](#api-4), a named test already holds the control. The fix only has to carry the rule and the test name into the spec. Also, several owning pages already state the principle in the right place. `specs/cli/stops.md:22` says that "other stop metadata cannot establish that independent work may continue". A fix can add the missing list or code next to such a sentence and does not need to restructure the page.

To fix the class, write each enforced rule on its owning spec page with its refusal code and the test that holds it. Then reduce the decision or record text to a link. Extend the inventory tests so that each column the code holds, such as a stop's removal attestation, is compared with the spec. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the details.

## 4. Legibility, objectivity and redundancy

This section answers the second question: where the text can be more legible and more objective, and what it repeats. The findings here are mostly patterns: a legibility lane read a page in full and reported each form that costs a reader, with a count, examples and a rewrite of one real passage.

| Class | Section | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sentence form | [4.1](#41-sentence-form) | 0 | 22 | 139 | 161 |
| Words: ambiguity and vocabulary | [4.2](#42-words-ambiguity-and-vocabulary) | 1 | 70 | 122 | 193 |
| Restatement | [4.3](#43-restatement) | 0 | 19 | 112 | 131 |
| Structure, budgets and routing | [4.4](#44-structure-budgets-and-routing) | 0 | 50 | 80 | 130 |
| **All** | | **1** | **161** | **453** | **615** |

### 4.1 Sentence form

The specs state their rules in the present tense, and most rules are correct. The defects come from the shape of the text: one sentence often carries many rules, and outcome matrices are written as chained prose. On the destroy, recovery and secret paths, a few sentences cannot be parsed at all, so an agent must guess the rule or read the code.

The audit found 161 findings in this class: 22 Medium and 139 Low, none High. Of them, 55 are single defects of the text and 106 are patterns reported with a count. 115 are new, 5 were already reported by audit 004 and are still present, 1 is tracked by an open item, and 40 Low findings have no judged status. Seven were found by more than one lane. The baseline shows the scale: 479 normative sentences (4.0%) are above 60 words, and in the X10 sample only 48% of sentences state exactly one rule ([section 2.5](#25-sentence-form)).

| Area | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| API | 0 | 27 | 27 |
| CLI | 5 | 17 | 22 |
| CEPH | 5 | 13 | 18 |
| REC | 4 | 12 | 16 |
| CTX | 0 | 12 | 12 |
| MOS | 2 | 9 | 11 |
| Other ten areas | 6 | 49 | 55 |

The API pages hold the most findings, but all of them are Low. Fourteen of the 22 Medium findings sit in CLI, CEPH and REC, on the pages where rules carry effects.

**Sentences that cannot be parsed on a safety path.** [REC-31](#rec-31) (`specs/state-reconciliation.md:2014`) says "The destroy record carries a source block IDs before its first effect": a word is missing, and the reader cannot tell which IDs a destroy record must hold before a retry. [REC-28](#rec-28) (`specs/state-reconciliation.md:1932`) decides which inverses a replacing destroy may skip, and only the code shows its meaning. [SEC-10](#sec-10) (`specs/secrets.md:447`) runs three hold conditions into one sentence. [SEC-25](#sec-25) (`specs/security.md:727`) lets a character-set qualifier attach to either of two clauses on an SSH configuration line, so one reading admits an unrestricted value. [REC-P6](#rec-p6) (`specs/state-reconciliation.md:1131`) hides the controller-stage edge rule that D251 states clearly.

**Decision tables written as prose.** [MOS-P2](#mos-p2) (`specs/managed-os.md:696`) and [OCP-P4](#ocp-p4) (`specs/openshift-clusters.md:1064`) give the Unknown resolution outcomes as chains of "Otherwise" and "Anything else". No reader can check that every case is there, and no test can cite a row. [SUB-P5](#sub-p5) (`specs/substrates.md:2298`) writes the pre-boot refusal catalog as one 259-word sentence and names two codes that do not exist. [CEPH-P19](#ceph-p19) (`specs/ceph-native-api.md:257`) links a "daemon-type table" that is not a table: its rows are spread over five paragraphs. [CLI-P16](#cli-p16) (`specs/cli/commands.md:432`) states the `--authorize` token grammar as one 36-line paragraph, and its dry-run scope reads two ways.

**Nested proofs on the erase path.** [MOS-P6](#mos-p6) (`specs/managed-os.md:1320`) puts the `%pre` root-target proof into paragraphs of 700 to 1,000 words with forward references. A coder who skips one conjunct erases the wrong disk.

**Rationale inside rules.** [REC-P2](#rec-p2) (`specs/state-reconciliation.md:2841`) mixes the derivation of a size bound, the reason for a boot flag and nine external links into the erase rule, so an agent cannot tell the requirement from the reason.

The cause is visible in the findings. Rules grow by adding clauses to the sentence that already exists, not by adding rows or items: [HAR-39](#har-39) counts 125 of 240 sampled sentences that state two or more rules, and [ARC-40](#arc-40) shows a rule run onto the end of an unrelated line. The garbled sentences in REC-31 and REC-28 read like clauses that lost a word in such an edit. The corpus conventions budget bytes per section ([section 2.4](#24-units-of-loading-sections-and-budgets)) but set no rule for sentence form and no rule that an outcome matrix is a table. No test holds either.

Two things are right and should stay. First, the corpus states rules in the present tense and almost never uses modal verbs: "should" appears 7 times and "shall" never ([section 2.5](#25-sentence-form)). Second, the best passages already show the house style: one rule per sentence, an actor, a code, a fail-closed outcome and often a named test. A short example from `specs/cli.md:803-805`:

> A root lock or context lease that cannot be acquired fails `context.busy`, naming the safe retry; Bootwright never takes a lease over.

Others are the bound with its count rule, code and test at `specs/api/networks.md:107-110`, the closed SSH ingress forms at `specs/api/machines.md:43-58`, the ordered kubeconfig export refusal table at `specs/cli.md:1309-1318`, and the controller refusal table that a test holds at `specs/api/environment.md:564-596`.

The rewrite that REC-31 recommends shows the fix on one sentence and keeps every fact:

> The destroy record carries a source block IDs before its first effect.

> Before its first effect, the destroy record lists the IDs of the source blocks whose proof it defers.

The class is fixed by a rule of form for new and touched text: one rule per sentence or list item, and a decision table for any outcome that depends on several observed states. The rewrite starts with the unparseable sentences on the destroy, erase and secret paths, then applies the rule to each page when it is next edited. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the checks.

### 4.2 Words: ambiguity and vocabulary

The audit found that the corpus uses many words as terms but defines few of them. The glossary is small, and some of its definitions are false. The cost is guessing: an agent reads one word in two senses, or reads a value it must act on that has no meaning. Most defects are Medium or Low. One is High, because scripts are told to act on values that nobody defines.

**The numbers.** The class holds 193 findings: High 1, Medium 70, Low 122. Of them, 169 are single defects of the text and 24 are patterns of form reported with a count. 105 are new, 23 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, 1 is tracked by an open item, and 64 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. 29 were found by more than one lane. Five areas hold most of them:

| Area | High | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| CTX | 0 | 10 | 17 | 27 |
| CEPH | 0 | 12 | 14 | 26 |
| CLI | 1 | 11 | 13 | 25 |
| API | 0 | 7 | 17 | 24 |
| MOS | 0 | 8 | 11 | 19 |

The vocabulary lane measured the glossary itself ([section 2.10](#210-vocabulary)). It has 22 entries. Five of its six "always" statements fail, and three of eight "never" statements fail. Of 28 load-bearing terms that the glossary does not define, 17 are used with two or more meanings.

**What the defects look like.**

- The stop vocabulary lists Level, Cause, Fault and Recovery values with no meaning ([CLI-4](#cli-4), [CLI-P1](#cli-p1), [CLI-50](#cli-50)). The Recovery row at `specs/cli/stops.md:33` is a bare list of nine tokens. `specs/cli/output.md:546-548` says a script acts on `cause` and `recovery`. The catalog then gives the same remedy, destroy and apply again, three different Recovery values. Only Certainty, at `specs/cli/stops.md:30`, has a definition for each value.
- The glossary closes Evidence and Receipt with "always" lists that the corpus breaks ([GOV-1](#gov-1)). `specs/glossary.md:103-104` says Evidence is "always" one of three kinds, but other pages use ownership evidence, erase receipts and build receipts. An agent that trusts the list reads an erase receipt as a lifecycle receipt.
- "Owner" has three senses on authorization paths: the product owner, the owning spec section, and Bootwright as owner of resources ([GOV-P2](#gov-p2)). "Operator" and "user" have no entry, see `specs/glossary.md:3`.
- "Refusal" names two events in the runner rules ([ARC-13](#arc-13), [ARC-14](#arc-14)). `specs/architecture.md:1083` says an attempt is `unknown` "after a refusal" but does not say if this is the adapter's `refused` phase or the runner's refusal of a record. The code treats them in different ways. The same word problem shows in domain Refusal tables: their role reasons are not the stop codes that operators see ([MOS-36](#mos-36), `specs/managed-os.md:2440-2441`).
- One word changes sense inside one section. In `specs/managed-os.md`, "registration" means both plan registration and RHSM subscription registration ([MOS-22](#mos-22), `specs/managed-os.md:1099`). "Stage" names four objects on `specs/contexts.md`, whose opener says no staging directory exists ([CTX-P18](#ctx-p18), `specs/contexts.md:7`). "Retire" means opposite things in spec and code on the removal path ([REC-68](#rec-68), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2549-2550`).
- A rule sentence reads wider than its owner means it. "A token the invocation does not require is inapplicable and refuses with `authorize.unneeded`", read literally, refuses every rebind, erase and abandon token ([REC-84](#rec-84), `specs/state-reconciliation.md:3052-3053`).
- Judgement words stand in for checks. On `specs/ceph-coverage.md:138`, "qualified" and "supported" have no observable meaning, and "qualified" collides with the glossary's own use of the word ([CEPH-P2](#ceph-p2)). In the complete-graph invariants, `agree`, `consistent` and `compatible` say no fields and no refusal path ([API-P13](#api-p13), `specs/api/ceph.md:378`).
- Some rule sentences have no acting subject, or a pronoun many lines from its antecedent ([HAR-10](#har-10), `specs/openshift-clusters.md:439-442`).

**Why it happens.** Terms are coined where they are first needed and are not taken back to the glossary. None of the 28 load-bearing terms the lane checked has a glossary entry, and only 9 have a definition in place. The glossary tries to close a word with an "always" list, and later pages add new kinds without editing that list. The same causes repeat over time. All 9 vocabulary findings of audit 004 that the lane sampled are still present ([section 2.10](#210-vocabulary)). The 23 known-004 findings of this class show the same thing.

**What is right and should stay.** The Certainty row at `specs/cli/stops.md:30` is the model: each value has a short meaning in the table, next to the field. Some glossary entries hold across the corpus, such as the bare word controller, BMC, and segment versus network. The convention that a term has one meaning and one owner page (C9) is sound; the text does not follow it.

**What fixes the class.** Each term that a rule relies on gets one owner entry with a definition that a test can check. A word with many kinds gets a generic definition and a list of examples, not an "always" closure. Every value an operator or a script acts on gets a meaning in its table. A word that carries two senses is split into two words. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the details.

### 4.3 Restatement

The corpus restates many rules in other words instead of linking their owner. Most copies still agree with the owner today, so most findings are Low. The cost is double reading, and each copy can drift. The Medium findings are the places where a copy already left out or changed part of the rule.

The audit holds 131 findings of this class: 19 Medium and 112 Low, none High. Of them, 86 are single defects and 45 are patterns of form reported with a count. By status: 57 are new, 55 are Low findings nobody judged, 16 were already reported by audit 004 and are still present, 2 are settled and 1 is tracked. Ten were found by more than one lane.

| Area | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| API | 3 | 29 | 32 |
| MIL | 1 | 16 | 17 |
| CLI | 2 | 13 | 15 |
| CEPH | 5 | 9 | 14 |
| OCP | 0 | 9 | 9 |
| REC | 0 | 8 | 8 |
| CTX | 2 | 5 | 7 |
| other eight areas | 6 | 23 | 29 |

The detector of near-verbatim copies finds only 53 clusters and 3,213 redundant bytes across pages. The drift sweeps estimate about 212,500 bytes restated outside the owner, and in 134 of 752 compared facts one page has drifted ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)). The lens B lanes estimate that 9% to 22% of each normative unit is removable, and 33% for one unit of deferred designs. These are the lanes' own estimates.

What the defects look like:

- [CEPH-57](#ceph-57): `specs/ceph.md:1244-1247` states the proof for physical Ceph retirement as verified erase receipts for every selected disk. Only the third statement, 150 lines later, carries the erase relaxation. An agent that reads only the first part builds a verifier that refuses `erase=<machine>:retain` and blocks the documented exit for a host that cannot be reached.
- [HAR-12](#har-12): the controller-to-BMC trust rule is stated on four pages. `specs/substrates.md:2117` restates it without a link to the owner. An agent that reads only that paragraph can miss the refusal of an unverified BMC for erase.
- [SEC-P4](#sec-p4): the confirm-before-lease protocol is stated in full once and restated in shorter, differing words for rotation, renewal and delete. The outcome list at `specs/secrets.md:809-813` leaves out encryption rotation.
- [CEPH-16](#ceph-16) and [CEPH-P20](#ceph-p20): the NVMe-oF placement rule appears twice on one page. `specs/ceph-native-api.md:557-559` refuses only a `count` below the host count, while `specs/ceph-native-api.md:1034-1035` says the count "must match", which also refuses a higher count. The implementer must choose.
- [CTX-P2](#ctx-p2) and [CTX-P5](#ctx-p5): the selecting condition of each controller package closure is written in three places and named in five more (`specs/controller.md:25`), and the `iputils` wording has drifted. The host-reservation key grammar has two full owners (`specs/contexts/controller-record.md:99-110` and `infrastructure-services.md`).
- [CLI-P8](#cli-p8) and [CEPH-P13](#ceph-p13): hand-kept copies already differ from their owner. The help rule at `specs/cli/commands.md:256-260` names the one-cluster rule for `--secrets` but not for `--object-user`. The `ceph.unsupported-release` row at `specs/cli/stops.md:476` drops a clause of the `ceph.md` row it copies.
- [MIL-55](#mil-55): each M4 section restates the acceptance profile that `add-on-coverage.md` owns (`specs/milestones/m4.md:147`). One copy names B755 and B757 as the operator gate where the owner names B1125.
- [GOV-7](#gov-7): `specs/project.md:106-113` restates the last-package wait set that `add-ons.md` owns, with a pending-decision marker. When the decision is answered, three pages need an edit.
- Large Low patterns: [CLI-P17](#cli-p17) finds columns and boilerplate remedies that repeat another column in about 13% of `specs/cli/stops.md`, with 107 instances. [CEPH-P22](#ceph-p22) restates one block-realization skeleton in prose 45 times. [MIL-112](#mil-112) finds delivered records that restate spec behavior at length.

Why it happens: a domain page restates the owner's rule in its own context so that the section reads alone, instead of linking the owner's anchor. The corpus almost never copies a sentence, but it often paraphrases one ([section 2.7](#27-repetition)), so the copy is not word for word and no check sees the drift. Inside long pages, a rule is stated in prose and again in a refusal table or field row ([API-P1](#api-p1), [CEPH-P7](#ceph-p7)). Hand-kept lists with no test that holds them to the catalog or the code drift first ([CLI-P8](#cli-p8), [CTX-P2](#ctx-p2)).

What is right and should stay: some restatements link their owner, and the audit judged them harmless, for example the host-reservation bounds in [API-P7](#api-p7). A named test, `TestCephRefusalTableMatchesUnsupported`, holds the Ceph refusal table. That is the right model for a table that must exist in two forms.

What fixes the class: each rule keeps one owner section, and every other statement becomes a link to its anchor with at most a short pointer. Where a copy holds facts the owner lacks, as at `specs/ceph-native-api.md:1031-1036`, those facts move to the owner first. Hand-kept lists move to the code or get a named test. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the details.

### 4.4 Structure, budgets and routing

The corpus holds the right rules, but an agent often cannot reach the one it needs without loading a whole page. The index names pages where it promises sections, the largest sections have no headings to narrow to, and some links and owners point to the wrong place. No finding of this class is High or Blocking. One cluster sits close to the safety path, though: the routes to the destructive and authorization rules.

The audit found 130 findings in this class: 50 Medium and 80 Low, none High. 66 are single defects of the text and 64 are patterns of form. By status, 84 are new, 20 were reported by audit 004 and are still present, 14 are tracked by an open item, and 12 are Low findings whose status nobody judged. 13 were found by more than one lane. Five areas hold the most:

| Area | Medium | Low | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| API | 4 | 14 | 18 |
| CEPH | 9 | 5 | 14 |
| CLI | 3 | 9 | 12 |
| MIL | 3 | 9 | 12 |
| HAR | 5 | 6 | 11 |

The other eleven areas hold 63 findings between them. CEPH holds the most Medium findings (9); CTX and HAR follow with 5 each.

**The index routes to pages, not owners.** [HAR-1](#har-1) shows that 27 normative pages above 24 KB are routed as whole pages, 2.38 MB in all (`specs/index.md:19`). The controller row names install, uninstall and the controller stage, which each have their own section, but it links the 91 KB page. Of 30 traced questions, 17 land on the right page with no section named ([section 2.2](#22-how-an-agent-reaches-a-rule)). [HAR-5](#har-5) is the heaviest case. The index names "mutation safety" but routes the whole 213 KB reconciliation page, and its Sections row omits `#physical-disk-safety`, `#confirmation-and-authorization` and `#mutation-safety` (`specs/index.md:23`). An agent can change a destructive path without reading the rule that makes it fail closed. [GOV-2](#gov-2) adds five normative pages that have no index route at all (`specs/index.md:5`).

**A link resolves to the wrong table.** `managed-os.md` has five headings named "Refusal table". All 13 links to `#refusal-table` open the Provided OS updates table, not the installation refusal table ([MOS-19](#mos-19), `specs/managed-os.md:2111`). An agent that looks for the FIPS, proxy or subscription rows finds none there and may invent them. `make docs-check` passes, because the anchor exists.

**Large sections have no inner structure.** Ceph's "Resources, readiness and access" is 45 KB with no level-3 heading, and it holds about sixteen block contracts ([CEPH-P5](#ceph-p5), `specs/ceph.md:1543`). The same shape repeats in contexts' 38.7 KB storage section ([CTX-P7](#ctx-p7), `specs/contexts.md:234`) and in the 87 KB managed-OS Installation section ([MOS-P4](#mos-p4), `specs/managed-os.md:212`).

**Owners are split or misplaced.** Three deferred pages hold admission rules that the code enforces, and the API pages defer to them ([DEF-7](#def-7), `specs/deferred/custom-playbooks.md:9`). An agent that reads them as proposals may loosen a safety refusal. The libvirt capacity gate has two owners that defer to each other ([SUB-13](#sub-13), `specs/substrates.md:1159`).

**The milestone read route has no bound.** The milestone opening budget covers only the opening. "And what they link" then pulls in open-decision leaves of 16 to 24 KB that no budget measures ([MIL-1](#mil-1), `AGENTS.md:8`).

The cause is visible in the findings. The budgets measure units by heading, and the corpus avoids that measure in two ways. It grants dated exceptions: seven sections and seventeen leaves, none removed in four weeks, while item B965, which owns the split, is parked ([section 2.4](#24-units-of-loading-sections-and-budgets)). And it writes text the budget does not see: 50 level-2 sections carry more than 8 KB of their own text ([HAR-27](#har-27)), and bold lead-ins stand in for headings 197 times ([HAR-34](#har-34)). The index cannot grow to name sections, because its file budget leaves 53 bytes of room ([HAR-1](#har-1)). So routing falls back to whole pages.

Some of this is right and should stay. The over-budget units are exactly the named exceptions, so the gate catches new growth. Where the index does name an anchor of a bounded section, the route works: the attempts and Ceph bootstrap questions land on their owner in one hop.

The fix is structural, not editorial. The large sections need splitting into headed leaves an anchor can reach, so the exceptions can be retired. The index then needs a route to the owning section of each task, the destructive owners first. A map of sections at the top of each large page gives that route without growing the index. Duplicate headings need unique anchors, and the rules in deferred pages need to move to the pages that own them. [Section 7](#7-the-plan) owns the order and the details.
