<a id="cli-40"></a>**CLI-40 Lifecycle receipt is called exactly four lines, but a failed operation writes a fifth `stop:` line.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source A.cli-output-1, S5-cli-contract. specs/cli/output.md:133 says the lifecycle receipt is exactly four lines, output.md:942 calls it 'the final four lines', and specs/glossary.md:108 calls it 'the four final lines'. <a id="cli-42"></a>**CLI-42 Plan `checks` enumeration names two kinds, but plans also carry `deferred`, `removal-evidence`, stage and `destroy-admission` checks.** Medium; error; text and code differ; new; source A.cli-output-1. <a id="cli-43"></a>**CLI-43 Stop remedies name context-backed commands without --context, against output.md's remediation rule.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: CLI-62); source A.cli-stops-2. output.md:557-565 makes a registry default that names a context-backed command carry `--context`, and the test checks only the defaultRemediations map. stops.md:13-14 says a stop's remedy defaults to its row's, and Stop.Fail copies the row remedy into Remediation before WithRemediationFor runs, so that function never adds a context to it. <a id="cli-46"></a>**CLI-46 No rule keeps secrets that native tools print out of retained adapter output; no_log covers only tasks that read bound material.** Medium; gap; proof, authorization or bound; new; source X9b-secrets-trace. The broad invariant already exists at specs/security.md:648-651 (every task, result and diff that could carry secret material uses `no_log`). In specs/security.md:1012-1014, replace 'every task that receives bound material sets it' with a link to that rule.

Replace 1416-1420 with: "A run whose file cannot be created, held or made durable fails before its adapter runs, names no file and removes any file it created, even when interrupted." <a id="cli-48"></a>**CLI-48 Bounded-run remediation names the attempt command, which cannot read a run.** Medium; error; a page contradicts itself; new; source A.cli-output-3. specs/cli/output.md Bounded run output says an adapter failure points its remediation at the run's file by the operation-attempt reader `bootwright logs --context <context> --operation <id> --block <block> --raw --attempt <N>`. <a id="cli-49"></a>**CLI-49 Stop definition says apply or destroy only, yet the catalog registers warnings and stops of other commands.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; new; source A.cli-stops-1, A.cli-stops-2, C.cli-stops-2. stops.md:6-7 and glossary.md:60-61 define a stop as a way an apply or destroy ends without completing its verb, and stops.md:14-16 says its certainty decides the attempt's outcome. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:6-7` "A stop is a declared way an 'apply' or 'destroy' ends without completing its verb: a refusal, a failed ..."; `specs/glossary.md:60-61` "- **Stop**: a declared way an 'apply' or 'destroy' ends without completing its verb, with one code, its ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:695`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/stops.md's opening, which owns the term, define a stop as a declared diagnostic of a Bootwright command, an error or a warning. State that its certainty decides an attempt's outcome only when it fires inside an apply or destroy attempt. Keep the glossary entry as a one-line summary that links to the stops page.

<a id="cli-50"></a>**CLI-50 Level, Cause and Recovery tokens are listed but never defined, and explain derives 'Repeat helps' from them.** Medium; gap; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source A.cli-stops-1, C.cli-stops-1. Rows in similar situations get different recovery tokens (authorize.unneeded fix-then-repeat for dropping a flag; erase.install-network 'authorize' with a remedy that names no token). The values matter: explain prints 'Repeat helps' as Recovery == repeat, and output.md:546-548 tells scripts to act on cause and recovery. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:29-33` "| Recovery | 'repeat', 'fix-then-repeat', 'change-input', 'other-verb', 'wait', 'authorize', ..."; `internal/cli/explain.go:31-32` "Recovery: string(stop.Recovery), Repeat: stop.Recovery == diagnostics.RecoveryRepeat, Meaning: stop.Meaning, ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:157`. **Fix:** In the Stop vocabulary of specs/cli/stops.md give each Level, Cause and Recovery value a one-clause definition as Certainty has (for example change-input: edit the desired state and import it; fix-then-repeat: change the environment or the invocation, then repeat the same command;

<a id="cli-51"></a>**CLI-51 Rows whose certainty contradicts the vocabulary's definition.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; new; source A.cli-stops-1. The vocabulary defines certainty 'possible' as 'an effect may be partial and a repeat converges it' and 'none' as 'nothing began'. engine.resolved-unperformed is 'none' although its meaning says the observation 'left part done'. Seven 'possible' rows carry recovery 'none' or 'abandon-context', where a repeat converges nothing: engine.produced-name-invalid, clients.evidence-unencodable, records.evidence-unreadable, records.state-unrecognized (recovery none), and erase.evidence-mismatch, install.guest-policy-unmet, operations.record-invalid (abandon-context). Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:30` "| Certainty | 'none': nothing began; 'possible': an effect may be partial and a repeat converges it; ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:108` "| 'engine.resolved-unperformed' | resolution | none | target | - | repeat | an observation proved a frozen ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:246`. **Fix:** Two changes. (1) Vocabulary, specs/cli/stops.md line 30: define certainty only by what may be on the target and let Recovery say what converges it, e.g. '`possible`: an effect may have begun and be partial; the Recovery field names what converges it'. Do not split the value. (2) engine.resolved-unperformed: the code raises one stop for two certainties.

<a id="cli-52"></a>**CLI-52 libvirt rows of certainty `possible` promise the `unproved` behaviour 'observes the host before anything else starts'.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; new; source C.cli-stops-1. `libvirt.outcome-unusable` (line 380) and `libvirt.postcondition-unproved` (line 381) have certainty `possible`, so their attempt is recorded `failed` and retried, yet their remedy says the repeat 'observes the host before anything else starts'. Under the spec, observation before any other step belongs only to unproved blocks. The Go declarations match the catalog, so the wording is the defect. They are the only `possible` rows with this remedy wording; the baremetal and kubevirt equivalents read 'observes the machine again'. The finder's count of other rows (13) is low, but that does not affect the claim. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:30` "'unproved': the effect must be observed before anything else starts"; `specs/cli/stops.md:15` "attempt's outcome: 'unproved' leaves it 'unknown', every other certainty"; `specs/cli/stops.md:381`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/stops.md and internal/substrate/libvirt/stops.go together, either make libvirt.outcome-unusable and libvirt.postcondition-unproved `unproved`, or change their remedy to 'repeat the operation, which observes the host again' as the baremetal and kubevirt rows read.

<a id="cli-53"></a>**CLI-53 Warning rows break the stop definition and output.md's rule that stop diagnostics carry cause and recovery.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; new; source A.cli-stops-1, X5-glossary-terms. The Warnings rows of specs/cli/stops.md:192-203 'end no verb', which contradicts the page's own definition of a stop (stops.md:6-7: a way an apply or destroy ends without completing its verb), and specs/cli/output.md:546-548 says any diagnostic raised from a stop carries cause and recovery, while warned() in internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/stops.go:310-311 emits only severity, code, message and remediation. So the Certainty, Cause and Recovery cells of the five warning rows reach only explain, and output.md's promise is wrong for them. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:194-195` "They carry the row's code and end no verb."; `specs/cli/output.md:546-548` "raised from a stop also carries, after 'remediation', 'cause' and"; `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/stops.go:310-311`. **Fix:** Keep the warning rows in specs/cli/stops.md (B1563 moves codes into the catalog, so do not move them back to output.md). In the Warnings intro state that a warning carries the row's code and remedy only as given by the raiser, takes no default remedy and emits no cause or recovery, and that its Level, Certainty, Cause and Recovery cells are shown only by explain.

<a id="cli-54"></a>**CLI-54 Certainty is assigned inconsistently: 'ended without proving its postcondition' is `unproved` in some packages and `possible` in others.** Medium; ambiguity; a page contradicts itself; new; source C.cli-stops-1. Certainty is assigned inconsistently for the same event, an adapter ending without proving its postcondition. It is `unproved` for firewall, osupdate, mirror and power, and `possible` for baremetal, libvirt and kubevirt. In lines 1-413 there are 11 `*-unproved` codes carrying `possible` or `none`; ceph.fips-unproved, past the lane, is a twelfth. The Certainty row defines each value but gives no rule for choosing one. `erase.evidence-mismatch` is `possible`, defined as 'a repeat converges it', yet its recovery is `abandon-context`. `baremetal.addresses-undeclared` is an input refusal with certainty `possible`. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:398` "'firewall.unproved' | block | unproved | target | - | repeat | the host firewall adapter ended without ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:361` "'baremetal.postcondition-unproved' | block | possible | target | - | repeat | the machine adapter ended ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:30`. **Fix:** Add one selection rule to the Certainty row in specs/cli/stops.md (when an adapter ended without proving its postcondition the stop is `unproved` unless the capability states why a retry converges it without observation first) and reclassify or rename the outliers: erase.evidence-mismatch (possible with abandon-context) and baremetal.addresses-undeclared (possible for an input refusal, should be `none`).

<a id="cli-55"></a>**CLI-55 ceph.retirement-refused default remedy says to 'erase every selected Ceph disk'; the code's remedy says to declare erasure authority.** Medium; unsafe-rule; text and code differ; new; source A.cli-stops-2, C.cli-stops-2. The ceph.retirement-refused row (specs/cli/stops.md:486, mirrored by Remedy in internal/storage/ceph/stops.go) says 'retain this context and erase every selected Ceph disk'. Both raisers (physical.go:84, physical_retirement.go:180) give a different remedy: retain the context and declare every selected data, DB and WAL disk in a hardware.dataDisks entry 'as originally applied, with a non-retain onRemoval'. The row remedy is what `explain` prints and what Stop.Fail uses when a raiser gives none, so the catalog and the code's own remedy diverge. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:486` "| 'ceph.retirement-refused' | removal-phase | none | input | - | change-input | a physical Ceph host holds no ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:487` "| 'ceph.retirement-unavailable' | operation | none | input | - | change-input | the planned Ceph cluster ..."; `specs/ceph.md:1108-1111`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/stops.md:486 and the cephRetirementRefused declaration, set the remedy to the raisers' text: 'retain this context: automatic retirement needs every selected data, DB and WAL disk in a hardware.dataDisks entry of each Machine, as originally applied, with a non-retain onRemoval'. change-input is wrong, because a post-apply change is refused as input.changed-since-apply.

<a id="cli-56"></a>**CLI-56 machine.enrollment is certainty `none` ('nothing began') but fires after the enrollment worker changed the host.** Medium; error; a page contradicts itself; new; source C.cli-stops-2. machine.enrollment is declared operation / certainty none ('nothing began') / recovery repeat (internal/machine/stops.go:30, stops.md:538). Yet refused() raises it after mutating work. In worker.go:37-69, manage runs the account worker in its mutating mode and raises enrollment-refused on an unrecognized state. In worker.go:72-92, prove runs after manage (capability.go:272-276), when the managed login and its sudo grant already exist. So 'nothing began' is false for these firings, and the attempt is recorded failed, not unknown. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:538` "| 'machine.enrollment' | operation | none | input | - | repeat | a provided Machine's enrollment could not ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:30` "| Certainty | 'none': nothing began; 'possible': an effect may be partial and a repeat converges it;"; `specs/api/machines.md:760-761`. **Fix:** Split the stop in internal/machine/stops.go and in its row in specs/cli/stops.md. Keep `machine.enrollment` as `none` for refusals raised before the worker runs: credential, authentication method, password. Add a post-worker stop of certainty `possible` with recovery `repeat` and a remedy such as 'repeat the operation, which observes the account before changing it'.

<a id="cli-57"></a>**CLI-57 Machine placement stop meanings cover only access.ssh, but the code also raises them for the access.lifecycle sudo arm.** Medium; error; text and code differ; new; source A.cli-stops-2. The catalog rows machine.placement-escalates (stops.md:544) and machine.placement-key-missing (:542) describe only the access.ssh arm, but internal/machine/placement.go dedicatedPlacement also raises them for the access.lifecycle arm: escalates for a lifecycle login that is not root/direct or non-root/sudo (placement.go:136-138), key-missing for a missing lifecycle privateKeyRef or knownHostsRef (:147-149), the latter a case the catalog otherwise files as placement-host-key-missing. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:544` "| 'machine.placement-escalates' | operation | none | input | - | change-input | a Machine that hosts ..."; `specs/api/machines.md:650` "| 'privilege' | enum | 'direct' requires user 'root'. 'sudo' requires a non-root user with noninteractive ..."; `specs/cli/stops.md:542`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/stops.md:542-544 and internal/machine/stops.go, widen the two Meanings to cover both arms. placement-escalates: 'declares a login whose account and privilege a placement does not admit: an access.ssh account other than root or an escalation Secret, or an access.lifecycle login other than root with direct or a non-root account with sudo'.

<a id="cli-58"></a>**CLI-58 `command.unconfirmed` covers cancellation in the stop catalog, but cli.md says a cancellation names no command.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source S5-cli-contract. The stop row for command.unconfirmed says the confirmation 'was declined, canceled or could not be asked' with remedy 'repeat the command with --yes', while cli.md:274-280 says a cancellation names no command in next: and never states which code a cancellation uses (it lists declined, non-interactive and unanswerable under the command's own code). The code uses command.unconfirmed for a cancellation with remedy 'repeat the command to be asked again', not --yes, so the stop row's single remedy is wrong for the canceled case and cli.md leaves the code unstated. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:626` "the confirmation an apply or destroy asks for was declined, canceled or could not be asked, so nothing began ..."; `specs/cli.md:280` "repeated with '--yes' in 'next:'; a cancellation names no command. The". **Fix:** In specs/cli.md:276-280 state the code of a cancellation: 'a cancellation refuses under the same code and names no command in `next:`' (this matches confirmation.go). Name confirmation_test.go as the test that holds it. In internal/cli/stops.go, drop the `--yes` remedy's claim to cover cancellation: either remove 'canceled' from the Meaning, or phrase the Remedy as 'after a decline or a non-interactive refusal, ...

<a id="cli-59"></a>**CLI-59 input.added-since-apply describes 'an apply in progress', but an additive apply builds on a completed apply.** Medium; error; two pages disagree; new; source A.cli-stops-2, O.CTX-1. The Meaning of input.added-since-apply (specs/cli/stops.md:634, and identically internal/workspace/contexts/stops.go:12) says imported input declares more than 'an apply in progress' froze, but the owning rule defines an additive apply as one over a completed apply (state-reconciliation.md:157-158, admission requires the completed apply and its blocks done), and contexts.md:200-203 raises this warning only for changed input over a completed apply. Evidence: `specs/cli/stops.md:634` "| 'input.added-since-apply' | context | none | input | - | repeat | imported input declares more than an ..."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:157-158` "An 'apply' over a completed apply under a changed input is an additive apply when the input only adds add-on ..."; `specs/contexts.md:200-203`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/stops.md:634 and the matching Meaning in internal/workspace/contexts/stops.go, which the catalog closure test keeps equal, change 'more than an apply in progress froze' to 'more than the completed apply froze, only add-on instances,'. Leave the Recovery class to the vocabulary definitions of the recovery-class finding (n 1) rather than changing it here.

<a id="cli-135"></a>**CLI-135 The Ceph bound-Secret value bound (one line, 1 to 1024 bytes of UTF-8) is stated only in a stop remedy, and the stop's meaning generalizes an SMB-only check.** Medium; gap; rule missing from the specs; new; source O.CLI-2. specs/ceph-native-api.md:852-853 says binding time checks the CephSMBResource password value's UTF-8 encoding 'and its bound' without stating the bound. The bound (one line, 1 to 1024 bytes of UTF-8) appears only in the remedy of the ceph.secret-invalid row (stops.md:489). That row's meaning, 'a Secret bound to a Ceph resource', is wider than what the code raises it for, which is only the CephSMBResource password binding. Evidence: `specs/ceph-native-api.md:852-853` "An authored password at either leaf refuses; binding time checks the value's"; `specs/cli/stops.md:489` "a Secret bound to a Ceph resource is not a value the adapter can lend | bind a Secret holding one line of 1 ..."; `internal/storage/ceph/smb_materials.go:21`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph-native-api.md, replace 'binding time checks the value's UTF-8 encoding and its bound.' with 'binding time refuses `ceph.secret-invalid` unless the value is one line of 1 to 1024 bytes of UTF-8 text.' In specs/cli/stops.md:489, narrow the meaning to 'a Secret a CephSMBResource binds is not a value the adapter can lend' and keep the remedy.

<a id="cli-136"></a>**CLI-136 'The dashboard password alphabet' is never defined, and the same page says Ceph's native policy, not Go, generates the dashboard password.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source O.CLI-2. No spec defines 'the dashboard password alphabet' or 'dashboard-alphabet characters'. cluster-admin-credentials.md:102-103 and ceph.md:1781 use the term for the 32-character monitoring candidates. The same page (lines 91-92) says Ceph's native password policy, not Go, generates the dashboard candidate, so the name points at an alphabet the dashboard candidate does not use. The alphabet exists only in code: dashboardAlphabet, 64 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ ., which also validates custodied values. Evidence: `specs/cli/cluster-admin-credentials.md:102-103` "The Prometheus and Alertmanager candidates are 32 characters of the dashboard"; `specs/cli/cluster-admin-credentials.md:91-92` "Its native"; `specs/ceph.md:1781`. **Fix:** State the alphabet once in specs/ceph.md (management gateway unit): 'a generated monitoring password is 32 characters drawn uniformly from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `-`, `_` and `.` (`dashboardAlphabet` in internal/storage/ceph/produced.go)'. In specs/cli/cluster-admin-credentials.md:102-103, link that sentence instead of saying 'the dashboard password alphabet that Go generates', and use the same name on both pages.

<a id="cli-137"></a>**CLI-137 output.md makes the power entry check sound optional ('can observe ... when the approved runtime is available'), but the owner makes it mandatory and fail-closed.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source O.CLI-2. The Preflight section of specs/cli/output.md (the `apply --dry-run` and `destroy --dry-run` preview) says a new lifecycle operation 'can observe Machine power when the approved runtime is available'. It does not say whether an unproved reading in the preview is a failed prerequisite, and it neither links nor names the owner. It does not weaken the execution gate: the mandatory, fail-closed power reading is owned by state-reconciliation.md#power-before-a-new-apply-or-destroy and the catalog row lifecycle.start-power. The owner does not itself name that code. Evidence: `specs/cli/output.md:716` "Machine power when the approved runtime is available."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2512` "The operator stops every managed target Machine before starting either flow."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2517`. **Fix:** In specs/cli/output.md#preflight, replace 'A new lifecycle operation can observe Machine power when the approved runtime is available.' with 'A new apply or destroy proves Machine power under power before a new apply or destroy.' In that owner section, name the code: 'A failed or ambiguous reading refuses the complete flow with `lifecycle.start-power` before any registration, ...'.

<a id="cli-139"></a>**CLI-139 The power.unproved catalog remedy names `bootwright machine status`, a command that does not exist; cli.md and the code name `machine list --power-status`.** Medium; error; stale reference; new; source L.names. Its remedy names the exact commands: a management controller that proved no ..."; `specs/cli/commands.md:155`. **Fix:** Change the Remedy of powerUnproved in internal/machine/power/stops.go to "read the power state again with bootwright machine list --context &lt;context> --power-status, then repeat the command" and update the catalog row at specs/cli/stops.md:214 to match. <a id="cli-140"></a>**CLI-140 Ceph retirement stop rows: hosts-survive covers only virtual hosts, and retirement-unavailable names no trigger.** Medium; gap; text and code differ; new; source O.CLI-3. The stops.md row for ceph.hosts-survive describes a cluster removed while hosts outlive the destroy, and gives a remedy about removing Bootwright-owned virtual host Machines. In the specs/cli/stops.md ceph.hosts-survive row, add the physical case to the meaning ('or physical hosts whose erase-backed retirement the frozen erase policy does not authorize') and to the remedy, linking ceph.md#devices-and-destructive-ownership.

Patterns of form:

<a id="cli-p1"></a>**CLI-P1 Vocabulary table defines only Certainty; Level, Cause, Fault and Recovery values are bare lists.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source B.cli-stops; 35 instances counted. The Stop vocabulary table defines each Certainty value. For Level (7 values), Cause (11), Fault (8) and Recovery (9) it gives only bare names. The one exception is `unclassified`, which line 35 explains, so 34 values have no meaning. No other spec page and no Go comment defines them. specs/cli/output.md:546-548 makes `cause` and `recovery` machine output 'so a script acts on them without parsing the code', which makes the missing meanings matter to callers as well as to implementers. Examples: `specs/cli/stops.md:29`; `specs/cli/stops.md:30`; `specs/cli/stops.md:33`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept with an amendment. In the specs/cli/stops.md vocabulary, give every value of Level, Cause, Fault and Recovery a one-clause meaning in the form the Certainty row already uses, stated as the operator's next step (Recovery) or as the point where the stop ends the verb (Level). The finder's Recovery meanings are a reasonable draft, but the owner must confirm each one. For example, decide whether `abandon-context` covers 'take the context back with destroy' (rows 450, 452, 454) or only restoring records and deleting the context. Add the rule: 'every value of a catalog column has a meaning here.'

### 10.6 State reconciliation

<a id="rec-1"></a>

#### REC-1 Six 'adapter gave no usable outcome' stops are certainty `possible`, so the block is recorded `failed`; the engine says such an outcome is recorded `unknown`

High; contradiction; failure behavior not stated; new; source C.cli-stops-2, X9d-unknown-continuation.

**Claim.** Six domain stops for an adapter that ended without a usable outcome (install.no-outcome, openshift.outcome-unusable, kubevirt.outcome-unusable, service.outcome-unusable, baremetal.no-usable-outcome, libvirt.outcome-unusable; specs/cli/stops.md lines 301, 320, 340, 360, 380, 449) are declared certainty `possible`. The catalog header (stops.md:14-16) and state-reconciliation.md:640-643 both say a stop that is not `unproved` records the attempt `failed`. Yet the capability returns outcome `unknown` with these stops, and the engine's adapter-outcome table maps `unknown` to block `unknown`, which is what the code records. Two spec rules therefore give different answers for the same firing. Siblings with the same meaning (addon.outcome-unknown, ceph.result-invalid, runner.no-result) are `unproved`. The finder's harm scenario (a `failed` block that a destroy never observes) does not happen in the code today. The defect is that the certainty column and the header rule mislead anyone who implements or reasons from the catalog.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:633-636`: "An outcome outside this set, and 'abandoned' from a capability, is"
- `specs/cli/stops.md:14-16`: "attempt's outcome: 'unproved' leaves it 'unknown', every other certainty"
- `specs/cli/stops.md:449`: "| 'install.no-outcome' | block | possible | defect | - | repeat | the installation adapter reported no usable outcome after it ran | repeat the operation, which observes the installation again |"
- `specs/cli/stops.md:616`: "| 'addon.outcome-unknown' | block | unproved | defect | - | repeat | the add-on adapter ended without an outcome the block can settle on | repeat apply to observe its objects |"
- `specs/cli/stops.md:505`: "| 'ceph.result-invalid' | block | unproved | defect | - | repeat | a Ceph adapter returned an outcome or a value it never produces | repeat the operation, which observes the Ceph state again before anything else starts |"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:642-644`: "running its effect. A failure a capability reports leaves its attempt 'unknown' when one of its diagnostics is a stop of certainty 'unproved', and 'failed' otherwise;"

**Impact.** A block whose effect may have run is recorded `failed`, not `unknown`. A later fresh destroy then takes it back by its inverse without first observing it by its apply observation (state-reconciliation.md:782-784 warns that a `failed` block is never observed by a destroy, so its inverses could delete the only copy of produced material). A continuation retries it with no resolution. An implementer cannot tell which certainty the engine requires. The remedy 'repeat the operation, which observes ... again' also promises an observation that a `failed` block never receives.

**Recommendation.** In specs/cli/stops.md set the certainty of kubevirt.outcome-unusable (301), openshift.outcome-unusable (320), service.outcome-unusable (340), baremetal.no-usable-outcome (360), libvirt.outcome-unusable (380) and install.no-outcome (449) to `unproved`, the same as runner.no-result, ceph.result-invalid and addon.outcome-unknown. Change the declared Stops in code in the same commit, because the catalog is held to the code. The rule stays in state-reconciliation.md#attempt-outcomes (lines 642-645). Add nothing there.

**Verification.** refuter: narrowed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands; merges 2 candidates.

<a id="rec-2"></a>

#### REC-2 The controller-dependency rule is garbled at the point that decides a refusal

High; error; text and code differ; new; source A.reconciliation-2, C.reconciliation-2.

**Claim.** The controller-dependency sentence at specs/state-reconciliation.md:1129-1134 cannot be parsed, and line 1151 is elliptical. The text is also wrong, and the finder's proposed rewrite repeats or adds errors. (a) The engine refuses a controller block's bad dependency with `plan.controller-order`, not `controller.unsupported`. (b) Blocks whose capability is ControllerIndependent, and the controller block's own ancestors, do not get the dependency on the controller block. (c) Line 1151 means that an explicit selection holding `controller` also admits the blocks the controller blocks wait for (their precursors). It does not mean that an explicit selection admits the controller blocks a selected block waits for.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1130`: "requirements resolve, each block depends on each controller block, whose"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1131`: "clients run its adapters, but what it waits for: a controller block, run"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1132`: "first, or one its capability runs without them, past the first after an"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1151`: "selection admits every stage, and 'controller' what its blocks wait for."
- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:8582`: "that it runs without the stage's clients ('lifecycle.ControllerPrecursor':"
- `specs/controller.md:614`: "selects. It is one block in that context's lifecycle plan, or two when its"

**Impact.** The sentence decides a refusal code and the plan's dependency edges, so implementers could disagree on both. One reading makes every block depend on every controller block. Another exempts blocks whose capability runs without the controller clients. A third orders the two artifact-mirror controller blocks. These were lines changed after the previous audit and have never been reviewed.

**Recommendation.** Rewrite specs/state-reconciliation.md:1129-1134 to match DependOnController. (1) Controller blocks are ordered among themselves by their dependencies. (2) A controller block may wait only on blocks whose capability declares that they precede the controller, such as a managed artifact mirror's blocks. A controller block after the first may wait on such a block only if that block itself waits on an earlier controller block. Any other dependency refuses before registration with `plan.controller-order` (link specs/cli/stops.md). (3) Every other block depends on every controller block, unless it is one of that controller block's ancestors or its capability declares it independent of the controller, such as a Machine account or hardware block. At 1151, write: 'an omitted selection admits every stage; a selection that includes `controller` also admits the blocks its controller blocks wait for' (stage.go:162-169 computes these precursors only when controller is selected).

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands; filed as Medium; merges 2 candidates.

<a id="rec-74"></a>

#### REC-74 The read-only runner rule lists a closed set of admitted operations that omits the credential preparation the code runs read-only

High; contradiction; text and code differ; new; source O.REC-1.

**Claim.** specs/state-reconciliation.md twice states a closed set of operations a read-only execution admits: observe, a lend, and the revoke of substrate-host-kubevirt-v1. Line 856 says the runner refuses every other operation there, and line 1509 says it refuses any adapter operation but those. The code also admits cluster-install-agent-v1/prepare_credentials and storage-ceph-core-v1/prepare_credentials as read-only entrypoints, and admin_credential_run.go marks the prepare_credentials run ReadOnly. No spec sentence other than the stop row names prepare_credentials. So the spec's closed list is wrong, and it is a hand-copied inventory that names a literal implementation id. TestReadOnlyEntrypointsAreExplicit holds the code's list, but no test holds the spec's.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:855-857`: "revoke, which the runner admits for 'substrate-host-kubevirt-v1' alone; it"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1508-1511`: "read-only: the runner refuses any adapter operation there but 'observe', a"
- `specs/cli/stops.md:183`: "the cluster's read-only preparation of an administrator credential update was not proved or returned no valid update, so nothing changed"

**Impact.** An agent who implements or reviews the read-only boundary from the spec would refuse the administrator-credential preparation and break `cluster admin-credentials` updates. Or the agent would treat the extra admitted entrypoints as an unreviewed widening of a privilege boundary. A future arm cannot learn from the spec how an operation becomes admissible in a read-only execution: the rule names one implementation instead of a capability-declared property.

**Recommendation.** In specs/state-reconciliation.md Plan and execution (1508-1511), state the rule once: a read-only execution admits `observe`, a `lend`, and the read-only entrypoints composition admits (`readOnlyOperations` in cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go, held by `TestReadOnlyEntrypointsAreExplicit`), and refuses every other adapter operation. Name the two kinds that set holds today by linking their owners: lent-access revoke (substrates.md#lent-kubevirt-access-revocation) and administrator-credential preparation (cli/cluster-admin-credentials.md). At 855-857, drop 'which the runner admits for `substrate-host-kubevirt-v1` alone; it refuses every other operation there' and link the single rule instead.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands.

Two different refusals in specs/state-reconciliation.md#record-encoding-and-versions are both called 'unsupported'. (1) A decoded operation record whose version is not operationstore.OperationVersion refuses operations.record-invalid, with abandon-context recovery (SR:555-556). Patterns of form:

<a id="rec-p1"></a>**REC-P1 Sixteen refusal codes are listed in one prose paragraph; several differ from the codes in cli/stops.md.** Medium; naming; two pages disagree; new; source B.reconciliation-3; 16 instances counted. specs/state-reconciliation.md:2926-2933 lists 16 erase refusal codes in prose and then says 'Each diagnostic is the stop of its code' (2938), which implies that these names are the stop codes. Six of them are adapter-level reasons that internal/managedos/physicalerase/refusal.go maps to differently named stops in specs/cli/stops.md: identity-mismatch and hardware-mismatch map to erase.target-mismatch, target-unanswered to erase.controller-unanswered, foreign-custody and custody-drift to ... Examples: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2926`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2932`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2938`; `specs/cli/stops.md:258`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. In specs/state-reconciliation.md, keep the rule that an erase phase reports one closed adapter code with a detail of only observed, non-secret values, and that the play stops outside `no_log`. Replace the 16-code prose and the per-code remedy clauses with a pointer to specs/cli/stops.md#physical-erase-stops. The stop table, which the code owns, gives each stop's remedy. If the adapter codes must stay visible, make the stop table the single place they appear: add an 'Adapter code' column to that table, filled from refusal.go and held by a test. Do not keep a second list. The prose then no longer misstates which remedies name the retain release; identity-mismatch also names it in code. Keep the custody-drift explanation (why no retain release, and the custody directory to remove by hand) only if the stop row's remedy does not already carry it.

<a id="rec-p2"></a>**REC-P2 Rationale, derivations and nine external source links sit inside rule text.** Medium; objectivity; sentence form; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: ARC-69); source B.reconciliation-3; 9 instances counted. The erase text in specs/state-reconciliation.md mixes rules with rationale, sourcing and delivery state. 2841-2844 gives the 160 MB/s and 14% derivation of the 896 GiB bound and advice ('should use metadataClear'). 2859-2863 explains why Anaconda's zram flag is insufficient. Nine external URLs act as authority (2793-2794, 2861, 2869-2876, 2892). Examples: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2841`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2862`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2869`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2922`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. In specs/state-reconciliation.md: (1) Delete the 'B70 remains subject to ...' sentence (2922-2924) and the 'Source review does not qualify ...' sentence (2877-2878). B70's milestone row and its delivered record own qualification state. Keep 'The boot media's frozen size and SHA-256 remain mandatory'. (2) Reduce 2840-2844 to the rule: 'A `logicalOverwrite` target larger than `machine.MaxLogicalOverwriteBytes` refuses at admission, in the frozen request and in the worker; a disk that cannot be written and read back within the worker deadline declares `metadataClear`.' Move the throughput and margin derivation to the B70 delivered record or a knowledge page. (3) Apply ARC-69's fix: move the image-construction mechanics (2852-2893, including the zram explanation and the dracut, RHEL, Anaconda and Lorax URLs) to the managed-OS physical-removal owner or to a knowledge page.

<a id="rec-p3"></a>**REC-P3 A rule says a name never proves ownership, then states the exception as present-tense fact beside a Not yet met paragraph that repeats it.** Medium; contradiction; delivery state or record shape; new; source B.reconciliation-3; 2 instances counted. Mutation safety states the invariant 'A name or controller record may locate a target but never proves ownership or identity' (specs/state-reconciliation.md:2474-2475) and carries a correct C3 'Not yet met ... tracked as B568' paragraph (2497-2498). Between them, a second paragraph (2488-2495) restates the same gap as present-tense fact ('A name still proves ownership in one known case'). Examples: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2474-2475`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2488`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2493`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2497`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept the main part, but not the B571 part. Move the hand-removal step for objects abandoned by an orphan-acknowledged deletion to B568's section in specs/milestones/backlog.md, or to the context-deletion remedy that owns it. Leave 2571-2572 unchanged.

Do not add a new spec table: the code and the existing test already own the inventory.

In specs/state-reconciliation.md 936-2466 'phase' carries two meanings, not three: (a) the removal phases of a destroy (pre-stop, online cleanup, host retirement), used at 952, 954, 2000, 2013, 2099-2100 and described only later at 2588-2620 (Quiescence before removal), with no link from 952; and (b) an undefined 'phase' of a scoped apply at 2065 ('A name must resolve to planned work in the current phase') and 2089 ('Review and authorize the resolved install in its own phase'), which matches ... Examples: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:952`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2065`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2089`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2099`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. <a id="rec-p6"></a>**REC-P6 Garbled sentences on ordering and admission paths force the reader to guess the rule.** Medium; ambiguity; sentence form; new; source B.reconciliation-2. The controller-stage ordering sentence (specs/state-reconciliation.md:1129-1134) cannot be parsed. It never says that the engine adds its edge only to blocks outside the controller block's ancestors, and it never names the flag an ancestor must declare (lifecycle.ControllerPrecursor). Both facts are clear in D251 (16) and in the delivered record. Examples: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1131`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1132`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1156`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1301`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept the rewrite of 1129-1134 using D251 (16): 'Once every requirement has resolved, the engine adds an edge to each controller block from every block that is not one of its ancestors, because the controller block's clients run those blocks' adapters. An ancestor runs before it only when its capability declares `lifecycle.ControllerPrecursor` (an artifact server placed over SSH and a managed artifact mirror's fill do). Any other ancestor refuses the plan with `controller.unsupported`, naming both blocks.' Change 1300-1301 to 'then run `bootwright apply --dry-run --context <name>`'. Rewriting the throttle clause is optional: 'and fewer running blocks name its throttle than that throttle's capacity'.

Keep the D146 and D283 links. The claim that a rule may carry no decision id is not a corpus rule; the owner would have to adopt it as a guidance change.

<a id="rec-p8"></a>**REC-P8 Heading does not say what the leaf decides: three leaves over budget bury unrelated subjects.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; already tracked (B965); source B.reconciliation-2. Three leaves of specs/state-reconciliation.md are over the 8,192-byte leaf budget: 'Stopping after an add-on instance' (12,773 bytes), 'Converging an effect' (10,407) and 'Continuation and removal' (20,582). ### 10.7 Contexts and the controller host

<a id="ctx-1"></a>

#### CTX-1 Removed `plan` command still named as a CLI verb and inside data-loss remedies

High; stale; stale reference; new; source A.reconciliation-2, S1-admission-freeze, X6-inventories.

**Claim.** No `bootwright plan` command exists: the CLI catalog (specs/cli/commands.md) and the code's commandSpec paths have no `plan`. Specs still name `plan` as a CLI verb (architecture.md:65), as a shared-lock reader (contexts.md:381) and as the reporter of host-port rows (managed-os.md:2505). The data-loss remedy placeholder `<digest bootwright plan prints>` appears in cli.md:289 and managed-os.md:920 and is the operator-facing constant lifecycle.DigestPlaceholder, which authorization.go and cli/repetition.go put into remedies. The destroy help text says the digest is what `bootwright destroy --dry-run` prints. cli/output.md:280 also names a context-free `media` command, but the command is `catalog media`. The pattern is wider than the 7 cited instances: controller.md:1230,1271, state-reconciliation.md:198,1244,1251,1288, api.md:32,41,43,48,67, openshift-clusters.md:34,99, add-ons.md:107 and api/addons.md all present `plan` as a command an operator runs. That is roughly 20 or more normative mentions.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:381`: "| shared | none | Every read: 'context list' and 'current', 'plan', 'status', 'logs' at each poll of an operation"
- `specs/architecture.md:65`: "| State reconciliation (CLI verbs 'plan', 'status', 'diff', 'apply', 'destroy') |"
- `specs/managed-os.md:920`: "'run bootwright destroy --authorize data-loss=&lt;digest bootwright plan prints>, which overwrites the declared"
- `internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/commands.go:76-77`: "const DigestPlaceholder = '&lt;digest bootwright plan prints>'"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1212`: "'--stage', and 'plan --until' previews the same selection."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1251`: "and the remedy, so 'plan' says why as 'apply' does; one refused for two"

**Impact.** On the data-loss authorization path, an operator copies a remedy and looks for `bootwright plan`, which fails as an unknown command. An agent that implements from contexts.md adds a `plan` reader to the lock table, or adds the command back. This is a stale name in operator-facing text on a destructive path.

**Recommendation.** specs/cli.md (Lifecycle receipts / authorization) owns the placeholder wording. It should read `<digest apply|destroy --dry-run prints>`, rendered from `lifecycle.DigestPlaceholder`, and the constant changes with it in its own commit. managed-os.md:920 should cite the cli.md owner instead of quoting the text again. Replace `plan` with `apply --dry-run` and `destroy --dry-run` in contexts.md:381 and managed-os.md:2505, and drop `plan` from architecture.md:65. In cli/output.md:280, change `media` to `catalog media`.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands; merges 3 candidates.

<a id="ctx-2"></a>

#### CTX-2 Fresh-install remedies omit deleting stored media, which uninstall requires; the record page says uninstall drops media

High; error; two pages disagree; new; source A.contexts-records, O.HAR-1.

**Claim.** Both fresh-install remedies on the controller-record page, and the matching code constants, tell the operator to destroy environments, delete contexts, then uninstall (--discard-unreadable, or --keep-packages) and install. Neither tells them to delete stored media first. The uninstall flow refuses a plain uninstall and a --discard-unreadable one while the media store holds any image, record or kept stage, because uninstall never deletes media the operator supplied. The page's sentence that the fresh install 'drops ... its stored media' contradicts that.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:122-124`: "contexts with their Secrets and its stored media, which 'bootwright context init'"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:166-169`: "running 'bootwright uninstall --keep-packages' and"
- `specs/controller.md:460-462`: "- a media store holding any image, record or kept"
- `specs/controller.md:444`: "a registry this build decodes that names any context or a media store holding any image, beside an unattributed entry too, still refuse as the plain uninstall does"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:114-119`: "record, destroy each environment and delete each context, then run this build's 'bootwright uninstall --discard-unreadable' and 'bootwright install'. Uninstall never reads the controller record,"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:119-124`: "because the store is readable and holds no context (uninstall flow). No command rebuilds the record alone: it is published by the first binding of an apply on a root that holds none, and a root holding one never gets a second. The fresh ..."

**Impact.** An operator who follows either remedy has uninstall refuse with a remedy they were not warned of. An agent that implements the record page as written would add the same incomplete remedy text. The claim that uninstall drops media also contradicts 'uninstall never deletes media the operator supplied'.

**Recommendation.** In specs/contexts/controller-record.md (Record and Bounds), make both remedies read: destroy each environment, delete each context and delete each stored image (`bootwright catalog media delete --name <image>`), then run uninstall (`--discard-unreadable` or `--keep-packages`) and install. Replace 'The fresh install also drops the host's contexts with their Secrets and its stored media, which ... recreate' with 'Recreate the contexts and media afterwards with `bootwright context init` and `bootwright catalog media add`.' Link the uninstall flow in specs/controller.md as the owner of what uninstall refuses instead of restating it. Record the matching code fix as an item; do not do it.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands; merges 2 candidates.

<a id="ctx-34"></a>**CTX-34 Controller relocation still said to wait on B103, but relocation was split out and delivered as the D184 rebind.** Medium; stale; stale reference; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: REC-39); source A.controller-2, C.controller-2. specs/controller.md:1068-1069 (Host identity) and specs/contexts.md:147-149 both say controller relocation waits on B103. The backlog's B103 (specs/milestones/backlog.md:448) says relocation was split out as B836. B836 was delivered in X164 with D184 as a root-confirmed rebind (delivered.md:8717-8720, 'bootwright controller rebind (D184) moves every context to a host whose...'). contexts.md:108 defines `bootwright rebind-host` (D184) as that explicit rebind. So the two specs point at the wrong item and suggest a delivered capability is missing. The availability claim is also not in the C3 form. Evidence: `specs/controller.md:1069` "relocation waits on B103."; `specs/milestones/backlog.md:448` "Controller relocation, left over from C16, was split out as B836 on"; `specs/contexts.md:108`. **Fix:** In specs/controller.md Host identity (line 1068-1069), replace 'controller relocation waits on B103' with 'a changed host identity is resolved by `bootwright rebind-host`'. Keep the restore-boundary link. Make the same replacement in specs/contexts.md:148-149, linking the rebind paragraph in the same section.

<a id="ctx-35"></a>**CTX-35 Host-coordination paragraph misstates which lock serializes prerequisites and whether a busy lock waits.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: ARC-08); source A.controller-2, S7-controller-host. The root-lock paragraph in specs/controller.md restates the lock model with drifted wording. 'A busy lock refuses' omits what the owner, specs/contexts.md, says: every mutator except uninstall waits (unlocked) up to the 1 minute root lock wait and then refuses context.busy, while uninstall, a reader taking its shared hold, and a lease refuse at once. The sentence 'Workspace serializes shared prerequisite mutation ... using its exclusive root lock' is also loose, because host package mutation is serialized by controller/install/lock, which the same paragraph names two sentences later. Evidence: `specs/controller.md:1080-1084` "Workspace serializes shared prerequisite mutation across every context in the fixed root using its exclusive ..."; `specs/controller.md:1084` "A busy lock refuses; there is no timeout-based takeover."; `specs/contexts.md:399-401`. **Fix:** Replace specs/controller.md:1080-1084 with one sentence: host prerequisite mutation is serialized by controller/install/lock, and root-lock and lease holds and waits follow the lock table. Keep only the rules specific to the setup lock (which actors take it, and that a launch holds its runtime's .lock shared).

<a id="ctx-36"></a>**CTX-36 Format-healing discard does not say what happens when a runtime lock is busy.** Medium; gap; failure behavior not stated; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: REC-38); source C.controller-2. The format-healing discard (specs/controller.md:1151-1155) says setup takes every runtime's lock first 'so it never removes one in use, and proceeds'. It does not say what happens when a lock is busy. The retention rule nearby (1176-1177) and controller-record.md:289-290 both say a runtime in use is skipped and kept. The code does something different for the discard: it refuses the whole discard with context.busy, 'a controller runtime is in use by a running command' (internal/workspace/contextfs/setup_linux_amd64.go:403-405, held by setup_linux_amd64_test.go:487). Evidence: `specs/controller.md:1153-1155` "taking every runtime's lock first so it never removes one in use, and proceeds. Because the discard removes ..."; `specs/controller.md:1176-1177` "'flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)' on its '.lock'; one a running command holds is skipped and kept, and setup reports ...". **Fix:** In specs/controller.md Format healing (line 1153), replace 'taking every runtime's lock first so it never removes one in use, and proceeds' with 'taking every runtime's `.lock` exclusively without waiting; a runtime a running command holds refuses the discard as `context.busy` and removes nothing (`TestDiscardRefusesWhileALaunchHoldsARuntime`); otherwise it proceeds'.

<a id="ctx-74"></a>**CTX-74 'A context's incarnation' is used on contexts.md without a definition, while state-reconciliation says contexts have no incarnation until B568.** Medium; naming; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source O.CTX-2. The context incarnation (device, inode and directory birth time or inode generation of the context directory) is defined only inside the OpenShift build-receipt paragraph of specs/openshift-clusters.md, and the code builds it that way. specs/contexts.md uses the term at line 854 with no definition or link, and specs/glossary.md has no entry. specs/state-reconciliation.md:2492 says B568 'gives each context a persistent incarnation', which reads as if none exists, while B568/D155 mean a separate persistent random identity carried by ownership markers. Evidence: `specs/contexts.md:854` "version does not move, and a context's incarnation keeps naming the recorded"; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2492` "B568 gives each context a persistent incarnation"; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2493`. **Fix:** In specs/contexts.md (Storage, locking and publication, at the directoryDevice paragraph), define the context incarnation in one sentence: the recorded device and inode of the context directory with its birth time, or its inode generation where no birth time is reported; it identifies executions and build receipts and enters no ownership marker. Add a glossary entry that points there.

<a id="ctx-75"></a>**CTX-75 Prerequisites table gives the host binding to `apply --stage controller`, but a context with no controller stage is bound by its first apply.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: CON-11); source O.CTX-2. The scope table in specs/controller.md lists the context-to-host binding among the Context prerequisites and names `apply --stage controller` as their owner. The same page says the controller stage never publishes a binding, and that a context with no controller stage has the binding as its only context check, settled by `apply --context <name>` whose first apply publishes it. specs/contexts.md says the first apply that uses the host publishes the binding before any reservation or effect. So the binding is no controller-stage prerequisite, and the table row contradicts the page. Evidence: `specs/controller.md:25` "the binding between this context and this host. | 'apply --stage controller' |"; `specs/controller.md:14` "that context's apply owns them. Each prerequisite belongs to exactly one side,"; `specs/controller.md:373`. **Fix:** In specs/controller.md, remove 'the binding between this context and this host' from the Context row and add a third row: '| Context | The binding between this context and this host | the context's first `apply`, before any reservation (binding) |'. Do not call it 'no prerequisite of either side': controller.md:373 already names it the context's only check, so it stays a context check with its own owner;

<a id="ctx-76"></a>**CTX-76 Uninstall root qualification is placed 'after the packages' in one paragraph and 'before any effect' in another.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source O.CTX-1. The uninstall flow states the root qualification (a directory root:root owns, writable by no group or other, not a link, not a mount point, on its parent's device) in two places. Whether those refusals precede dnf removal is derivable only from test names (the code does check in the read-only view, before any callback). Evidence: `specs/controller.md:542` "**State.** After the packages, uninstall renames each root that exists aside"; `specs/controller.md:552` "device. Each root must first be a directory 'root:root' owns, writable"; `specs/controller.md:595`. **Fix:** In specs/controller.md#the-uninstall-flow, add one entry to the 'Refusals before any effect' list: each root that exists must be a directory root:root owns, writable by no group or other, not a link, not a mount point (a bind mount included) and on its parent's device, or uninstall refuses naming it, with TestAnUninstallRefusesAMountedRootOrStagingBeforeAnyEffect and ...

<a id="ctx-77"></a>**CTX-77 A context whose selection drops to the baseline runs no stage, so its binding keeps naming its old tool area.** Medium; gap; rule missing from the specs; new; source O.CTX-1. No passage says what clears a binding's `tools`, or retires its area, when a context whose binding already names a tool area is later planned with nothing beyond the host baseline. controller.md and state-reconciliation.md:1135-1137 say such a context contributes no controller block. The rule that clears `tools` ('a stage that selects no tool clears it') binds only a stage that runs, for example one that selects host packages but no tool client. The path is reachable: destroy, update to client-free input, apply. Evidence: `specs/controller.md:693-694` "A context that selects nothing beyond the host baseline contributes no block at all."; `specs/controller.md:729` "on the context's binding the area it proved, or none when it selects no tool,"; `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:67-69`. **Fix:** In specs/controller.md#the-controller-stage, change line 693-694 to: "A context that selects nothing beyond the host baseline contributes no block once its binding names no tool area; while its binding still names one, it contributes the block, which selects no tool, clears `tools` and retires what no binding names." Qualify controller.md:28 the same way, or link it to that sentence.

### 10.8 Security and secrets

<a id="sec-1"></a>

#### SEC-1 Elevated reveal commands do not check sudo's output I/O log; only stdin logging is guarded

High; gap; proof, authorization or bound; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: CLI-26); source X9b-secrets-trace.

**Claim.** The specs guard an elevated `secret set --value-stdin/--password-stdin` against sudo's input logging only (`log_input`, `log_ttyin`, `log_stdin`). No page says anything about sudo's output logging (`log_output`, `log_stdout`, `log_ttyout`). Yet every context-bound command, including the raw reveals (`secret show`, `cluster kubeconfig`, `cluster keyring`) and the structured reveals (`cluster info --secrets`, `--object-user`), runs as a UID 0 child through sudo and writes the secret bytes to standard output. A sudoers policy that turns on output logging therefore records every revealed value in sudo's I/O log, a sink the reveal contract never names or checks. The code follows the input-only rule: the privilege test passes a listing that sets only `log_output`.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/secrets.md:96-102`: "sets 'log_input', 'log_ttyin' or 'log_stdin' refuses with 'secret.input'"
- `specs/cli.md:1217-1218`: "'secret show', 'cluster kubeconfig' and 'cluster keyring' are raw"
- `specs/cli.md:1224-1225`: "log, history, cache, terminal title, or second stream. Callers are responsible"
- `specs/cli.md:310-313`: "Bootwright child as UID 0 through the qualified absolute sudo executable. Pin"

**Impact.** An implementer copies the input-log proof to `secret set` alone. A kubeconfig, an administrator password, CephX keys or S3 keys revealed under an output-logging sudoers policy then persist in sudo's I/O log directory, outside custody and its deletion rules. That is disclosure of secret material past the stated boundary.

**Recommendation.** In specs/secrets.md, next to the stdin I/O-log rule (lines 96-113), add one rule: an elevated sensitive reveal reads sudo's policy listing the same way, and before any custody read it refuses when the listing sets `log_output`, `log_stdout` or `log_ttyout`, or cannot be read. Use the same refusal-code family and the same remedy: a root login session that sudo did not start. specs/cli.md#resource-inspection-and-explicit-access links to that rule and does not restate it. Name the test that holds the rule.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands.

<a id="sec-2"></a>

#### SEC-2 secret delete is missing from the effect-material hold, so the hold can be bypassed

High; gap; proof, authorization or bound; new; source A.secrets, C.secrets.

**Claim.** The effect-material hold (specs/secrets.md:427-470) lists only generate --renew, a stale regeneration and a set replacement as refused writers. secret delete (line 153-158) removes the current mapping while keeping bound versions and has no hold refusal. Service.Delete in internal/secrets/custody/service.go never consults holds, and holdIndex.holder (holds.go:67-70) reports not-held once no current version exists. So delete followed by generate replaces a held effect-material Secret's only revealable version, which is the outcome the hold exists to prevent.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/secrets.md:153`: "'delete --name' removes an active mapping, including orphans, while retaining"
- `specs/secrets.md:430`: "effect-material Secret, nothing replaces the Secret's current version, because"
- `specs/secrets.md:432-433`: "current one is then the only copy the operator can read. 'secret generate --renew' or"
- `specs/secrets.md:433`: "a stale regeneration naming the Secret, and a 'secret set' replacement,"

**Impact.** An operator who deletes a held disk recovery passphrase or delivered host key loses the only copy any command can reveal, because show and every other command refuse bound versions. A later generate then replaces it silently while the effect still rests on the old version. An implementer who follows the text builds exactly this gap.

**Recommendation.** In specs/secrets.md, Effect material under a live binding, add delete to the refused writers: "`secret generate --renew` or a stale regeneration naming the Secret, a `secret set` replacement and a `secret delete` of it refuse with `secret.store.conflict` and write nothing, before any prompt or input read and again under the lease." Add a pointer from the delete paragraph (line 153), as generate has at line 139, and name a new test (for example TestDeleteRefusesALiveEffectMaterialBinding) in the test list at lines 463-470. The code fix is separate tracked work: Service.Delete must call refuseHeld.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands; merges 2 candidates.

<a id="sec-3"></a>

#### SEC-3 Inconclusive-removal retry restated without the owner's ownership and once-only conditions

High; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source A.security-1.

**Claim.** security.md:41-46 restates the replay-safe inconclusive-removal retry and drops the owner's condition that the block's owning apply durably recorded an attempt (ownership from durable records). The once-only condition is approximated by 'admits one retry' but not stated as the owner's 'no earlier resolution of the block in this operation was inconclusive'. The restatement links the owner, but an agent reading only security.md would permit the retry without durable ownership evidence.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/security.md:42-46`: "declares it replay-safe: a successful read that cannot tell its postcondition"
- `specs/security.md:44-45`: "from an unreadable target is recorded 'inconclusive', never 'no-effect', and"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:694-697`: "block's owning apply durably recorded an attempt of it, so its ownership comes"

**Impact.** The retry removes over a target the read shows. An agent that implements it from the security page would allow a removal retry without durable ownership evidence, or would allow repeated retries. That risks destroying something this context does not own.

**Recommendation.** Replace the restated sentence at specs/security.md:41-46 with: 'The one narrowing is the single replay-safe removal retry that resolution outcomes owns.' Restate none of its conditions there; state-reconciliation.md stays the owner.

**Verification.** refuter: narrowed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands.

#### SEC-4 Custom code section says authored add-ons are inert data that grant no privilege, but executable authored OLM add-ons now install operators with whatever privileges their CSV requests

High; stale; proof, authorization or bound; new; source A.security-2, C.security-2.

**Claim.** specs/security.md Custom code (1047-1058) says authored ClusterAddon declarations are declarative data that only Bootwright-owned code consumes, that custom packages gain the built-in lifecycle only with B90, and that no origin grants privilege authority. B90 is now 'awaiting operator acceptance, X235' (first slice: executable authored OLM add-ons). api/addons.md:108 installs an authored olm arm when a binding selects it. add-ons.md:25-27 says the author's catalog image and CSV are code the author chooses, and the operator runs with the privileges that code requests. add-ons.md:15-19 in the same section still says 'Authors cannot select executable code ... privileges'. The privilege-grant paragraph (security.md:1060-1070) covers built-in packages only. The owner page has gone stale against the delivered executable shape, and add-ons.md contradicts itself across two adjacent paragraphs.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/security.md:1048`: "declarative data that only qualified Bootwright-owned code consumes; built-in"
- `specs/security.md:1055`: "inventory, endpoint, dependency, credential, or privilege authority."
- `specs/add-ons.md:25`: "An authored OLM add-on's catalog image and ClusterServiceVersion are code the"
- `specs/api/addons.md:108`: "An 'olm' arm of the executable shape installs when a binding selects it, as one"
- `specs/security.md:1054-1055`: "inventory, endpoint, dependency, credential, or privilege authority."
- `specs/security.md:1064-1067`: "A built-in package grants privileges to identities it"

**Impact.** A security reviewer reading the owner page concludes that an authored add-on cannot select code or privileges. **Recommendation.** In specs/security.md Custom code, replace the 'declarative data' sentence and the 'only with B90' clause. <a id="sec-51"></a>

#### SEC-51 The Ceph registry login is classed as an access credential, yet an effect writes it to each host, and no spec says whether a rebind rewrites that file

High; contradiction; failure behavior not stated; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: REC-36); source O.SEC-1.

**Claim.** The pages agree that the Ceph registry login is an access credential that each host also keeps native-side in /etc/ceph/podman-auth.json (secrets.md:563-566, api/secrets.md:220). The 'effect material' reading is therefore excluded, and the claimed contradiction does not hold. A gap remains. state-reconciliation.md#access-credential-rebind lets a continuation of the Ceph cluster, host and image blocks rebind the registry login. No page says whether the continuation rewrites, or re-proves, each host's retained podman-auth.json, which cephadm uses for its own native pulls (ceph.md:1202-1206). Recovery proves that file only against recorded descriptor metadata, never against its contents (ceph-native-api.md:167-171). After a rotation and a rebind, an implementer cannot tell whether cephadm-initiated pulls must use the new login.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/secrets.md:563-565`: "login, an access credential, is also retained native-side: each Ceph host"
- `specs/secrets.md:389`: "created. An access credential is only presented to authenticate to an endpoint"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:3157-3158`: "their 'kubeconfigRef', the Ceph cluster, host and image blocks the"
- `specs/ceph.md:1205-1206`: "publishes, before its registry credential, a podman engine drop-in in"

**Impact.** An operator who rotates the registry password and runs `--authorize rebind=<secret>` can get a continuation whose cephadm-initiated pulls on each host still use the old login and fail. An implementer has to guess whether to refuse the rebind (effect material) or to rewrite the host file during the continuation.

**Recommendation.** The owner settles this in specs/state-reconciliation.md#access-credential-rebind, with no restatement elsewhere. Either (a) a rebind of the Ceph registry login republishes each host's retained `podman-auth.json` under its recorded intent before any native pull, which needs a named test; or (b) the host-retained login rests on its bound version as effect material: drop 'the Ceph cluster, host and image blocks the registry login' from the rebind list, so `authorize.rebind-invalid` names the host step. Record the choice as an item. secrets.md#native-side-retention then links to the chosen rule.

**Verification.** refuter: narrowed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands.

<a id="sec-22"></a>**SEC-22 runner.adapter-running is said to refuse 'only' for its own context, but an unattributable job refuses every context.** Medium; contradiction; a page contradicts itself; new; source A.security-1. security.md:361-363 says a run refuses with runner.adapter-running 'only while a job of its own context holds its lock', but 375-377 says an unattributable or holderless held job refuses a run of every context, without naming a code; the code returns runnerAdapterRunning for that case, so 'only' is wrong and the second sentence's code is unnamed. Evidence: `specs/security.md:361-362` "once none of them runs; a worker still being stopped keeps holding it. A run refuses with ..."; `specs/security.md:375-377` "bounded runs of two contexts proceed together. A held job whose record is". **Fix:** In specs/security.md, change 'and starts nothing, only while a job of its own context holds its lock' to 'and starts nothing, while a job of its own context, or a held job no context can be attributed to, holds its lock'. Name `runner.adapter-running` in the sentence at 375-377.

<a id="sec-23"></a>**SEC-23 'Every ssh client an adapter runs' includes the whole back end, yet Ceph and guest sessions reduce it.** Medium; contradiction; ambiguity or vocabulary; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: ARC-18); source A.security-1, X9c-privilege-trust. security.md:606-608 says every adapter ssh client and the runner's SSH arm read a generated configuration that 'includes the host crypto-policy backend and nothing else', without saying whole or reduced. The runner arm includes the back-end file whole; the Ceph, SMB and guest sessions (618-619) take it reduced to its crypto directives. The page never says which treatment a new adapter ssh client must use or why the runner arm is the unreduced one. This is an ambiguity, not a contradiction. Evidence: `specs/security.md:606-608` "Every 'ssh' client an adapter runs, and the runner's SSH arm, reads only a"; `specs/security.md:618-619` "The Ceph host, cluster and SMB blocks' controller sessions take the"; `specs/security.md:618-620`. **Fix:** In specs/security.md:606-608, scope the generic rule: 'reads only a configuration generated for that run: the runner's SSH arm includes the host crypto-policy back end; every other adapter-run client takes the back end reduced to its crypto directives, as below.' Making the runner arm reduce as well is a design change. Record it as an item and do not edit it into the text.

<a id="sec-24"></a>**SEC-24 Listener exposure promises 'serves only its declared consumers' and a 'trusted network' that nothing defines.** Medium; untestable; proof, authorization or bound; new; source A.security-1, C.security-1. Listener exposure states 'A listener serves only its declared consumers' and that a privileged listener binds loopback or a host-only address unless the operator 'explicitly places it on a trusted network', yet every managed listener in the table is a root container with host networking, DNSServer and ArtifactServer admit every reachable client, managed-os.md says these services admit every client reaching the selected zones, and neither 'trusted network' nor 'host-only address' is defined in the glossary or by any field. Evidence: `specs/security.md:661-663` "its Machine policy is external. A listener serves only its declared consumers. A privileged"; `specs/security.md:672` "Bind address and operator firewall; every reachable client can query and use declared forwarders"; `specs/managed-os.md:2369-2370`. **Fix:** In specs/security.md Listener exposure, replace 'A listener serves only its declared consumers. A privileged listener or one carrying cleartext credentials binds loopback or a host-only address unless the operator explicitly places it on a trusted network.' with 'Each managed listener binds only its declared addresses;

<a id="sec-25"></a>**SEC-25 The policy-line refusal sentence cannot be parsed, and the shared table names no test.** Medium; ambiguity; sentence form; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: ARC-18); source A.security-1, C.security-1. security.md:727-731 says 'A line of the backend that is not one allowlisted directive, or `GSSAPIKeyExchange no`, with a value of letters, digits and `@.,_+^*?!/ -` refuses', so the character-set qualifier can attach to either clause. <a id="sec-26"></a>**SEC-26 The supply-chain pin rule forbids floating tags for catalog snapshots, while the add-on API admits a catalog image by tag with polling.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source C.security-2. specs/security.md:807-813 requires add-on packages and catalog snapshots to be pinned by an immutable version and a content digest, and forbids floating tags during execution, with no exception. <a id="sec-27"></a>**SEC-27 Acquisition origins names three origin kinds, but the code and cli.md also class hosts as declared, vendor delivery and media store, and an unlisted public registry bypasses the image mirror.** Medium; contradiction; text and code differ; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: NEW-12); source A.cli-1, A.security-2. security.md Acquisition origins (specs/security.md:921-930) says every artifact comes from one of three origin kinds and defines no `declared` class. Drop the unpinned-release clause and the trust details, which the owner holds. Do not add a new restatement of the refusal.

<a id="sec-30"></a>**SEC-30 The no_log and management-controller refusal rule has three owners whose scope has drifted.** Medium; duplication; two pages disagree; new; source C.security-2. <a id="sec-31"></a>**SEC-31 'custom packages gain the built-in lifecycle only with B90' claims availability outside the Not yet met form, and B90 is already awaiting acceptance.** Medium; stale; delivery state or record shape; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: API-47, COR-33); source A.security-2, S10-add-ons, S13-scope-lifecycle, X3-not-yet-met. security.md:1051-1054 ties the custom-package lifecycle to delivery item B90 in a rule sentence ('custom packages gain the built-in lifecycle only with B90'). <a id="sec-52"></a>**SEC-52 FIPS fleet and host key rules state an RSA floor of 2048 bits, but Secret admission accepts no SSH private key below RSA-3072.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source L.numbers. specs/secrets.md admits an SSH private key only as Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA of at least 3072 bits, and the code enforces 3072 (validSSHPrivate). managed-os.md's FIPS rules for the fleet key (an sshKeyPair Secret) and the delivered physical host key (a Secret) state the floor as RSA of at least 2048 bits, so an RSA key of 2048 to 3071 bits is refused by Secret admission before the FIPS check runs. Do not restate the number. Leave specs/ceph.md:114 alone because it governs a pinned public host key.

Patterns of form:

<a id="sec-p1"></a>**SEC-P1 Decision and item ids, delivery state and decision rationale interrupt rules; one open item is not in the Not yet met form.** Medium; stale; delivery state or record shape; new; source B.security; 14 instances counted. Normative rules in specs/security.md carry delivery state, evidence history and mid-sentence decision ids. 'Verified TLS transport is delivered under B446' (695-696) and 'B318 records its in-tree evidence; B78 retains real-hardware qualification' (689-690) are delivery state written as rules. Decision ids sit inside definitions: 'D183, Q99' (110), 'D183, Q98' (123), 'as D152 and D248 amend it' with D248 not linked (81), and 'as D251 (41) decides' (964). Examples: `specs/security.md:695`; `specs/security.md:81`; `specs/security.md:332`; `specs/security.md:935`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept, amended. In specs/security.md: delete 689-690 from 'B318' on, and delete 695-696 (milestones own delivery evidence). Rewrite 325-332 so the rule reads 'A Ceph native worker ends its process group on SIGHUP, SIGTERM or SIGINT; a concurrent bootstrap is fenced by its attempt marker.' Follow it with 'Not yet met: a worker on a managed host survives a lost SSH channel that delivers no signal until its aggregate limit (640 seconds for a Ceph native worker, longer for a package or bootstrap worker), while the attempt already reads canceled or unknown; tracked as B573.' Replace '(D183, Q99)' and '(D183, Q98)' with nothing or one trailing link to D183. Link D248 or drop 'as D152 and D248 amend it'. Drop the '(41)' at 964. Keep linked reason citations such as D250 at 936.

<a id="sec-p2"></a>**SEC-P2 Implementation mechanics of the job directory, lock and sweep sit in one 83-line paragraph of Process boundary.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; new; source B.security; 9 instances counted. Process boundary (specs/security.md:256-446) is a level-2 section with no subheadings, 12,986 bytes. That is within the 24,576-byte section budget, and the 8,192-byte leaf budget does not apply to it because C10 counts only headings of level 3 or deeper. Lines 338-420 are one 83-line, 5,926-byte paragraph. Examples: `specs/security.md:338`; `specs/security.md:342`; `specs/security.md:397`; `specs/security.md:412`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. Keep the rules in specs/security.md, which owns them (14 inbound links to #process-boundary), and do not move them to architecture.md.
