The engine's online ordering says such a Machine, if still running, 'is stopped gracefully through its identified power path'. ceph.md's two-phase removal, which ceph.md says uses that engine ordering, says it requires 'explicit host shutdown' and that 'Neither phase authorizes powering off hosts implicitly'. substrates.md also says a KubeVirt-hosting removal 'pauses ... until the operator stops them'. So the corpus disagrees on whether Bootwright or the operator powers off a deferred Machine. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:2466-2468` "teardown completes. Neither phase authorizes powering off hosts implicitly."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2579-2580` "remaining deferred Machines. A deferred Machine still running is stopped"; `specs/ceph.md:1239-1244`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md, the target-removal paragraph at lines 2464-2468, replace 'then require explicit host shutdown and prove Machine quiescence ... Neither phase authorizes powering off hosts implicitly' with 'then prove Machine quiescence before any Machine or disk destruction; power changes during removal follow quiescence before removal'. The state-reconciliation section stays the one owner.

Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:2479-2481` "surviving host keeps the refusal below, and a bare-metal one retires only"; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2544-2547` "The engine supports the online ordering below. Candidate Ceph capabilities"; `specs/cli/stops.md:488`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md#removal-and-concurrency replace 'keeps the refusal below' with 'refuses `ceph.hosts-survive` with no effect', naming TestACephClusterWhoseHostsSurviveNamesItsOwnRemedy; in specs/state-reconciliation.md#quiescence-before-removal link that code instead of describing the refusal again.

<a id="ceph-69"></a>**CEPH-69 Ceph removal rules state delivery and qualification status outside the Not yet met form.** Medium; stale; stale reference; new; source A.ceph-4, C.ceph-4. <a id="ceph-70"></a>**CEPH-70 Tiebreaker refusal names do not match the stop catalog, and a 'no effect' refusal sits under an unproved code.** Medium; naming; two pages disagree; new; source T6-ceph-unreachable-host. specs/ceph.md names the refusals `tiebreaker-foreign` and `tiebreaker-unreachable` but never says that both are reasons under the single stop `ceph.tiebreaker-unproved` (certainty unproved). From the spec, an implementer could declare them as separate stops. The certainty is not a contradiction: 'with no effect' describes the refusal itself, and the code's message says earlier owned removal steps may already have completed, which justifies unproved. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:2540-2541` "else, an FSID-scoped part on an unclaimed host among it, refuses"; `specs/ceph.md:2579-2581` "tiebreaker is unknown, never absent, and refuses 'tiebreaker-unreachable'"; `specs/cli/stops.md:507`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md#a-provided-tiebreakers-removal state once that the reasons `tiebreaker-foreign` and `tiebreaker-unreachable` are raised as the `ceph.tiebreaker-unproved` stop. Reject the proposal to change the foreign case's certainty or give it its own row: that would change the decided behavior.

<a id="ceph-73"></a>**CEPH-73 The manager-restart tolerance sentence ('A failure is the command's own answer, and refuses as before, only when...') has no clear reading.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source A.ceph-4, C.ceph-4. The sentence 'A failure is the command's own answer, and refuses as before, only when the available manager it was sent to still holds one interval later, ...' uses 'as before' with no antecedent and 'one interval' with no definition in the specs (the code constant MANAGER_INTERVAL is 5 seconds). The sentence is wedged between cache-hold text and applies only to manager-served declarations. The finder overstates the ambiguity: 'until the manager wait ends' (2637) and 'A concurrent manager restart therefore never fails an unclaimed block' (2646) bound the reading, so a competent reader gets the intended rule. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:2642` "to each daemon it deploys, a sibling block's included. A failure is the"; `specs/ceph.md:2643` "command's own answer, and refuses as before,"; `specs/ceph.md:2644`. **Fix:** Move the sentence out of the cache-hold text into its own paragraph and rewrite it as the finder proposes. Name the interval after the code's constant, and do not invent a new bound.

<a id="ceph-130"></a>**CEPH-130 Closed service records follow one IBM build's schema, while the page says the selected release's native schema is authoritative.** Medium; ambiguity; a page contradicts itself; new; source O.CEPH-2. ceph-native-api.md opens with 'the selected release's native schema is authoritative' while four sections admit closed records whose members follow one IBM build's ServiceSpec schema 'the source read for these records, not a pinned build'. The page does not state in one place how the two combine. It partly resolves the split: Bootwright admission is the closed member set, and the selected image's own ServiceSpec normalization judges what remains and reports through `nativeError` (lines 36-37, 688-689; ceph.md:921-922 freezes native defaults from the selected image). Evidence: `specs/ceph-native-api.md:26-28` "is the comparison format; the selected release's native schema is"; `specs/ceph-native-api.md:388-389` "whose members and spelling follow IBM's python3-ceph-common 20.2.1-405 ServiceSpec schema (the source read ..."; `specs/ceph.md:921-922`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph-native-api.md's opening paragraph, state once: 'Admission's closed records are Bootwright's fixed member sets, read from IBM's python3-ceph-common 20.2.1-405 ServiceSpec schema; the selected release's schema is authoritative for defaults and for acceptance, so a member that release lacks or rejects refuses through `nativeError`.' Replace the four parentheticals with a link to that paragraph.

<a id="ceph-131"></a>**CEPH-131 'legacy incomplete ownership' in the lost-reply refusal list is undefined and reads as a refusal tailored to a historical shape.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source O.CEPH-3. specs/ceph-native-api.md:122 lists 'legacy incomplete ownership' among the lost-reply states that refuse. The phrase is not defined anywhere in specs/ (the only occurrence), and the Ansible code has no matching state (its only 'legacy' is the native host-directory layout refusal in ceph_native_observe.py). The reader cannot tell whether it means a Bootwright ownership record or a native layout. The finder's further claim that it is a tailored refusal for a historical shape under C11 is only one possible reading and is not established. Evidence: `specs/ceph-native-api.md:121-123` "missing result after an attempt, legacy incomplete ownership, changed scope or"; `specs/project.md:165-167` "converters, migrations, aliases, older readers, reader-version negotiation,". **Fix:** In specs/ceph-native-api.md, replace 'legacy incomplete ownership' with the observable native states it means: a host data directory other than the exact FSID, or a daemon that cephadm reports with style 'legacy' (foreign or native legacy layouts). Link the owning host-layout leaf. Do not add any rule about older Bootwright records.

<a id="ceph-132"></a>**CEPH-132 MDS service readiness counts 'its placement count' of daemons, which is undefined when the placement has no count.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source O.CEPH-2. The MDS readiness rule at specs/ceph-native-api.md:264 says 'its placement count of daemons' without naming the count for a placement that has none (hosts, label or host_pattern only). The sibling SMB rule (ceph.md:2027) names the fallback of one per placement host, and the worker uses count else len(hosts). The number is defined elsewhere only for admission (ceph-resources.md:733-735: 'the placed daemons are its resolved hosts, capped by `count`'). The same bare 'placement count' also appears in the rgw readiness rules (ceph.md:812, 2068). Evidence: `specs/ceph-native-api.md:264-265` "An MDS service is ready when its placement count of daemons runs with the"; `specs/ceph.md:2027` "daemons, as many as the placement count or else one per placement host, on the"; `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native.py:2730`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph-native-api.md (Service identity and references), replace the sentence with: 'An MDS service is ready when as many daemons as its placement `count`, or else one per frozen placement host, run with the frozen image; no active rank is required before its filesystem exists.' This matches ceph.md's SMB wording and the worker.

<a id="ceph-133"></a>**CEPH-133 CephClient states its single-client removal as a current rule, although D160 moved single-client revocation to B491.** Medium; contradiction; decision log; new; source O.CEPH-2. The CephClient section states, unscoped, that removal 'waits for declared consumers to be quiescent, revokes the owned principal and withdraws its material'. Every sibling family on the page says per-resource removal while the cluster survives is B491's and that the resource retires with its cluster's hosts. D160 (OD2 (a)) moved single-client revocation to B491, and the whole-cluster path for owned virtual Machines runs 'with no native call'. The CephClient sentence has no B491 pointer, so it reads as present online per-client revocation (an auth removal) that no code or other rule supplies. Evidence: `specs/ceph-resources.md:659-660` "Removal waits for declared consumers to be quiescent, revokes the"; `specs/milestones/m2.md:247` "D160 chose (a): move these clauses and B489's single-client revocation to B491"; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1749-1750`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph-resources.md#cephclient, replace 'Removal waits for declared consumers to be quiescent, revokes the owned principal and withdraws its material through the lifecycle transaction.' with: 'The principal and its material retire with the cluster; revoking one client while the cluster remains is B491's.' The quiescence and revocation duties stay only in B491.

<a id="ceph-134"></a>**CEPH-134 CephConsumer pre-offer check of external-details states no outcome when a check fails.** Medium; gap; failure behavior not stated; new; source O.CEPH-3. specs/ceph-resources.md (Consumer key custody, lines 1492-1503) lists the pre-offer checks of the assembled external-details but states no result of a failed check: no stop code, no attempt state, no statement that nothing is offered. Before offering them the block checks them: every key is a"; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1474-1476`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph-resources.md#consumer-refusals, add one row: a failed external-details check after the credentials exist refuses before the output is offered, offers nothing, names the failed check (for example the recorded leader that is no longer a declared MON at its address), and states the correction the owner chooses. Then name the test that holds it in #consumer-key-custody. Do not restate the check list;

<a id="ceph-135"></a>**CEPH-135 `registry-ownership` is specified as a named refusal but has no refusal entry, so it reaches the operator as the generic unknown.** Medium; gap; structure or routing; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: CLI-24); source O.CEPH-1. The spec does say what happens to `registry-ownership`. specs/ceph.md:963-965 states: "A token the block gives no remedy is published as `unknown`, or `remote-refusal` from a native worker, with the token in the detail". So the candidate's "the spec never says so" is false. What remains is a smaller problem. That fallback rule sits under "Bootstrap identity and continuation" (heading at ceph.md:833), about 260 lines away from "Named refusal outcomes" (ceph.md:1222-1235), which says only that "A named refusal of a Ceph block ends the attempt with its entry's code". Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:1212-1214` "The file is root's, its directory writable by root alone, and its record is durable before it; a name no ..."; `specs/ceph.md:1224-1225` "A named refusal of a Ceph block ends the attempt with its entry's code.". **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md, Named refusal outcomes, add one sentence: a token that has no entry ends the attempt unknown, through the block's generic `unknown` refusal, with the token in the detail. This resolves `registry-ownership` without a second owner. Then carry out CLI-24's fix: a Token | Code table held to the Go refusal maps by a test.

<a id="ceph-136"></a>**CEPH-136 Unbooted device-less OSD tolerance is not limited to this operation's clears, so a foreign one keeps the cluster unready with no exit.** Medium; gap; failure behavior not stated; new; source O.CEPH-1. specs/ceph.md (Devices and destructive ownership) tolerates every OSD whose metadata names no device and whose map entry never booted. Such an OSD counts against no declared disk instead of refusing `foreign-osd`, and it keeps the cluster unready, named as `unbooted@osd.<id>.<fsid>`. The tolerance is not limited to fsids that this operation's recorded clears name. Only fsids that completed owned clears report are purged. So an unbooted, device-less entry that Bootwright did not create skips `foreign-osd` and keeps the cluster not ready on every later apply. No refusal code or remedy names it. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:1501-1506` "observation, including the bootstrap state an apply reads before any host's OSD preparation, therefore counts ..."; `specs/ceph.md:1515-1520` "Each host's OSD preparation returns the OSD fsids of its completed clears, also once the disk holds an OSD of ...". **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md, Devices and destructive ownership, add the outcome for an unbooted OSD whose fsid no recorded clear names. Prefer that it refuse `foreign-osd`, keeping the tolerance only for fsids that a recorded clear intent of this cluster names. Use any recorded intent, not only this operation's, so that a later apply still finishes an interrupted purge.

<a id="ceph-137"></a>**CEPH-137 The `.rgw.root` claim is scoped to 'this operation's gateways' in ceph.md, but to the cluster in the resources page and the code.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source O.CEPH-2. ceph.md scopes the `.rgw.root` claim as one 'this operation's gateways share' (and the `.nfs` claim as 'this operation's NFS units recorded'), while ceph-resources.md:180-181 says the first gateway that proves it absent claims it and 'its sibling gateways share' it. The worker's claim is keyed by owner and FSID only, so it is cluster-scoped and operation-independent. The 'this operation' wording can be read as keying the claim by apply operation, which would refuse object-realm-foreign on a retry or continuation under a new operation. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:2047-2049` "under the claim this operation's gateways share through monitor commands only,"; `specs/ceph-resources.md:180-181` "absent claims and its sibling gateways share, the per-realm 'dashboard' system user"; `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/ceph_native_object.py:599`. **Fix:** In specs/ceph.md's gateway block, write 'proves `.rgw.root` absent or under the cluster's `.rgw.root` claim (owner and FSID), which every gateway of the cluster shares', and make ceph-resources.md:179-181 link that rule instead of restating it. Check the `.nfs` claim at ceph.md:1658 separately against its code.

Patterns of form:

<a id="ceph-p1"></a>**CEPH-P1 Delivery state, slice ids and decision codes are written into rules.** Medium; stale; stale reference; new; source B.ceph-resources; 64 instances counted. specs/ceph-resources.md writes delivery state and roadmap into its normative text. There is a **Current:** availability paragraph (9-22) and a target-ownership paragraph naming B80/B81/B477-B483/B489/B492/B474 (23-30). It also has 'once ... authored / until then' availability sentences (136-140, 1299-1301), 64 B-item mentions, ten D160/OD lines and a D159 clause (887). The online-removal deferral to B491 is restated per kind at 140, 464, 494, 823, 846, 947, 1514, 1522, 1542, 1559 and 1610. Examples: `specs/ceph-resources.md:23`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:823`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1299`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1428`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept with amendments, in specs/ceph-resources.md. (1) Replace the **Current** and target paragraphs (9-30) with present-tense statements. Give one C3 paragraph to each kind that is still unmet, for example the SMB samba-image refusal, which already belongs to ceph.md#refusal-table: link to it and drop 136-140/1299-1301. Then fix 1764. (2) State the retirement rule once in 'Shared resource contract': 'A resource is never removed while its cluster remains; it retires with its cluster's hosts.' Follow it with 'Not yet met: online removal of one resource while its cluster remains; tracked as B491.' Delete the per-kind copies. (3) Delete the stale sentence at 487-489, because the promotion record owns those refusals. Write the refusals as 'RBD namespaces, striping, object size and encryption are not fields and refuse `api.field`', and leave the decision codes to the backlog.

<a id="ceph-p2"></a>**CEPH-P2 'Qualified' and 'supported' are used undefined, contradict the page's own 'no vendor support table', and collide with the glossary's meaning of 'qualified'.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; new; source B.ceph-coverage; 56 instances counted. On specs/ceph-coverage.md, 'qualified' and 'supported' appear in several rule sentences with no observable meaning, so an implementer cannot turn them into code or a test. Examples: 'qualified privilege escalation' and 'qualified config and manager modules' (138), 'supported TPM2 variants' (139), 'supported EC data' (141), 'supported CephFS/RGW exports' (143), 'The qualified service mode defines ...' (159-161), 'qualified batching or pagination preserves snapshot identity' (175-176). Examples: `specs/ceph-coverage.md:138`; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:159`; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:175`; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:143`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. Do not add a glossary entry. Lines 23-30 already define qualification as evidence scope. In rule sentences, replace 'supported X' with 'X that Bootwright realizes' or 'X the native tools accept', whichever is meant, and replace 'qualified X' with the observable property. 175-176: 'Batching or pagination reads one snapshot, returns the complete inventory and never truncates silently.' 159-161: 'For each service mode, the acceptance record states whether clients continue automatically or need an explicit recovery action; a daemon-health pass alone never proves client continuity.' 58: 'an already-qualified public IP' becomes the property that was checked. The owner is this page, with the matrix families linking their item.

<a id="ceph-p3"></a>**CEPH-P3 About 42 refusal codes live only inside prose, with no table of code, trigger and effect state.** Medium; structure; no check holds it; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: CLI-24); source B.ceph-2; 42 instances counted. The apply-time refusal names of the Ceph blocks (sso-unverified, monitoring-login-unsupported, nfs-export-path-escape, pool-drift and others) appear only inline in prose. The spec neither links the code catalog that owns them nor holds them with a table. That catalog is adapterRefusals in internal/storage/ceph/materials.go, which pairs each name with its diagnostic code, reason and remedy; internal/storage/ceph/refusal_test.go maps names to codes. Examples: `specs/ceph.md:1576`; `specs/ceph.md:2727`; `specs/ceph.md:2783`; `specs/ceph.md:1817-1818`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. C6 says the code owns inventories, so do not hand-copy 42 rows. In specs/ceph.md 'Named refusal outcomes', add one sentence naming `adapterRefusals` in internal/storage/ceph/materials.go as the owner of every apply-time refusal name with its code, reason and remedy. Optionally add a docs check that every backticked refusal name in ceph.md is a key of that map. Keep the existing default that unlisted names leave the outcome unknown. Drop the finder's 'effect state (failed or unknown)' column: 1222-1233 already decides it.

<a id="ceph-p9"></a>**CEPH-P9 Single sentences carry whole algorithms or several rules (7 above 60 words, plus overlong paragraphs).** Medium; legibility; sentence form; new; source B.ceph-resources; 7 instances counted. Seven sentences on the page exceed 60 words: 225 (130 words), 412 (105), 795 (74), 1018 (73), 1494 (71), 178 (62) and 815 (62). The placement-group budget (412-424) writes a formula as prose, and that prose reads two ways on two points. First, whether the `.mgr` term applies to every rule or only to the cluster's pool rule. Second, what the bound is for a device-class rule. Examples: `specs/ceph-resources.md:412`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:225`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:795`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1494`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept, with a corrected formula. In specs/ceph-resources.md 'Placement-group budget', write the following. 'Before any effect, plan refuses a pool whose CRUSH rule's load exceeds its bound. Load(rule) = Σ pgNum × width over the cluster's pools on the rule (width = replica size, or k+m; a cephfsMetadata pool counts at least 16 placement groups). On the cluster's pool rule only, add: 1 × S for `.mgr`; 32 × S for each zone pool of each CephObjectGateway of the cluster; and 32 × S once for `.rgw.root` when the cluster has a gateway. S is the cluster default pair's size on `replicated_rule`, and 4 on a stretch cluster's rule. Bound(rule) = 250 × 3 for a rule restricted to a device class, else 250 × max(3, selected OSD count).' Split 225, 795 and 1494 into a lead line plus bullets, one refusal or proof per bullet, keeping the order at 795.

### 10.14 Add-ons

<a id="add-1"></a>

#### ADD-1 add-ons.md requires re-planning for another build's continuation; state reconciliation forbids it

High; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source S12-architecture-restated.

**Claim.** add-ons.md:199-202 says another build continues an add-on operation only when re-planning yields the same request. The continuation owner, state-reconciliation.md Dependency safety during recovery, says continuation never requires the current planner to reproduce the saved requests, and that it proves contract fingerprints and content digests and reads the frozen request instead. add-ons.md:187-188 gives a third rule for the same case, a 'block comparison', and links to Continuation and removal, which defines no block comparison. architecture.md:1324-1325 gives a fourth wording, 'only where that build freezes the same blocks', which also implies re-planning. The executor/planner partition test TestLifecycleExecutorNeverReplans supports the state-reconciliation reading.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/add-ons.md:202`: "only when re-planning yields the same request."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1370-1371`: "current planner to reproduce the saved requests, defaults, blocks or ordering."
- `specs/add-ons.md:187-188`: "by the block comparison."
- `specs/architecture.md:1324-1325`: "silently selecting one, and runs another build's automation only where that"

**Impact.** An agent implementing add-on continuation may re-render the package's program at continuation to compare requests. That brings planning into the executor, which the lifecycle partition test forbids. It may also refuse a continuation the content-digest proof would admit, or admit one that proof would refuse. This is on the recovery path.

**Recommendation.** Make state-reconciliation.md#dependency-safety-during-recovery the only owner. In add-ons.md:199-202, end the sentence at the digest: "...a change to what a package renders changes the request and its content digest; another build continues an operation only as dependency safety during recovery proves." In add-ons.md:187-188, replace the link text "block comparison" ... #continuation-and-removal with the same dependency-safety link, because that section defines no block comparison. In architecture.md:1324-1325, replace "and runs another build's automation only where that build freezes the same blocks" with that link.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands.

<a id="add-2"></a>

#### ADD-2 A transient failed read gets the remedy 'destroy and apply again', the same as a foreign object

High; unsafe-rule; failure behavior not stated; new; source C.add-ons, X9d-unknown-continuation.

**Claim.** specs/add-ons.md Observation and continuation (lines 463-471) treats a foreign object and a failed read the same way: both make the block unknown, and both get the remedy 'destroy and apply again'. A failed read in an observation can be transient. The general continuation rule says to continue the operation, which observes the block again. The code follows the add-on text: internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go returns the destroyAndApply remedy for both Ownership Foreign and Unknown, with the reason '... is foreign or could not be read'. lifecycle.unresolvedFailure then prints 'destroy and apply again, then repeat &lt;command> to observe it again', so an operator who sees one failed read is told to destroy a whole cluster.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/add-ons.md:467`: "foreign object or a failed read is unknown, whose remedy is to"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:589`: "| apply unknown | continue it, resolving every unproved block first and then retrying what resolution leaves 'failed' (D146)"
- `specs/add-ons.md:411`: "are read every ten seconds; a failed read while waiting is not yet a result,"
- `specs/add-ons.md:467-468`: "foreign object or a failed read is unknown, whose remedy is to"
- `specs/add-ons.md:468`: "destroy and apply again, except for an instance an"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1637-1639`: "admitted over it. Once the operator removes the foreign object or restores the"

**Impact.** An operator who follows the printed remedy after one unreachable API read destroys a whole virtual cluster and reinstalls it, when repeating apply or continuing the operation would have resolved the block. An implementing agent who copies the text keeps a destructive remedy for a condition that needs no destruction.

**Recommendation.** In specs/add-ons.md, Observation and continuation, split the unknown outcome. A foreign object keeps its current remedies: destroy and apply again, or for an additively added instance, remove or correct the object and repeat apply. A failed read is unknown with the remedy that state-reconciliation.md#resolution (lines 718-723) owns, the command that observes it again; link that section instead of restating it. Record an item for the matching change in internal/addons/instance/unresolved.go. Today both the Unknown-ownership branch and the fallback branch return destroyAndApply.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands; merges 2 candidates.

<a id="add-6"></a>**ADD-6 Left out still parks per-interface MetalLB forwarding that D246 adopted.** Medium; contradiction; decision log; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: API-32); source A.add-on-coverage. specs/add-on-coverage.md lists per-interface MetalLB forwarding (B776) as left out and cites Q34, whose answer (a) says the package makes no forwarding change. <a id="add-8"></a>**ADD-8 The stale-condition rule ('long after', 'never decides') can be built two ways.** Medium; ambiguity; ambiguity or vocabulary; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: REC-55); source C.add-ons. Readiness (specs/add-ons.md:413) says a condition 'unchanged long after its object's other conditions is reported as stale and never decides'. 'Long after' sets no threshold, and 'never decides' has two readings. The code takes one of them. ansible .../module_utils/cluster_objects_model.py:188-190 marks a condition stale when its lastTransitionTime is earlier than the latest lastTransitionTime among the object's conditions, with no threshold. It computes readiness without regard to that flag, so a stale True condition still satisfies the check. Evidence: `specs/add-ons.md:413` "object's other conditions is reported as stale and never decides.". **Fix:** Accept the finder's rewrite in specs/add-ons.md Readiness, as long as it matches evidence.go: 'A checked condition whose lastTransitionTime is earlier than the latest lastTransitionTime of the object's other conditions is recorded as stale in the evidence; staleness is a report and does not change whether the check holds.' Name the test that holds it.

<a id="add-9"></a>**ADD-9 Placement namespace for gitops is called the operator's namespace, but openshift-gitops is the Argo CD instance namespace.** Medium; error; text and code differ; new; source A.add-ons, S10-add-ons. Evidence: `specs/add-ons.md:442` "entry names as its operator's namespace (for 'gitops', 'openshift-gitops'),"; `specs/add-ons.md:593-594` "'Application' named 'bootwright-bootstrap' in the default instance's namespace 'openshift-gitops'"; `internal/addons/packages/gitops.go:15`. **Fix:** In specs/add-ons.md Owned Secrets, replace 'one the package's registry entry names as its operator's namespace (for `gitops`, `openshift-gitops`)' with 'one of the `placementNamespaces` its package declares (for `gitops`, the default Argo CD instance's namespace `openshift-gitops`)'.

<a id="add-30"></a>**ADD-30 add-ons.md says any instance added to an installed cluster goes in by additive apply; the owner admits only new bindings or new package members.** Medium; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source O.ADD-1. specs/add-ons.md says an instance added to a cluster the apply installed is installed by an additive apply, with no limit on how it was added. The owner, specs/state-reconciliation.md#additive-apply, admits only added ClusterAddonBinding objects, or bindings whose every changed path is a new spec.packages.&lt;member>. An added instance reached through an existing binding's addonRefs or profileRefs, through a new or changed ClusterAddon or ClusterAddonProfile, or through a profile edit keeps the changed-input refusal apply.not-an-addition. Evidence: `specs/add-ons.md:206-209` "completed apply; one added to a cluster the apply installed is installed by an additive apply, and repeating ..."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:169-172` "- the frozen revision compiles and the objects it differs from the selected input by are only added ...". **Fix:** specs/add-ons.md:207-208: replace 'one added to a cluster the apply installed is installed by an additive apply' with 'an input that only adds what an additive apply admits is installed by one'. The admitted shape stays only in state-reconciliation.md#additive-apply. The owner's opening sentence there ('only adds add-on instances') should also say that the admission list below defines that phrase.

<a id="add-31"></a>**ADD-31 Additive-apply admission says only bindings may be added, but the code also admits an added Secret that an added block places.** Medium; gap; text and code differ; new; source O.ADD-1. The additive-apply admission bullet (state-reconciliation.md:169-172) lists only added ClusterAddonBinding objects and new spec.packages members as the permitted difference, and never says that an added Secret is admitted. The same section later says the additive apply 'binds only the Secrets its blocks place' (:189-190). The code admits an added Secret only when an added block names it for the first time and no lineage block already references it. It refuses apply.not-an-addition for a Secret that no added block names or that a lineage block already names, and for a changed or removed Secret. Evidence: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:169-172` "- the frozen revision compiles and the objects it differs from the selected input by are only added ..."; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:189-190` "revision as its input, so a repeated 'apply' settles over it. It binds only the Secrets its blocks place, in ...". **Fix:** In specs/state-reconciliation.md#additive-apply, extend the second bullet: '...only added `ClusterAddonBinding` objects, added Secrets that an added block names and no lineage block references, or bindings whose every changed path is ...; an added Secret that fails this refuses `apply.not-an-addition`, naming it'. Name TestAnAdditiveApplyAdmitsOnlyANewSecretAnAddedBlockNames as the holding test (C13).

<a id="add-p1"></a>**ADD-P1 Delivery state sits in the coverage table, the qualification rules and a rule sentence.** Medium; stale; delivery state or record shape; new; source B.add-on-coverage; 24 instances counted. specs/add-on-coverage.md carries delivery state in normative text. Six '(delivered)' markers sit on lines 42 (2), 44 (2), 416 and 418. A 'Needs definition' cell sits at line 48. The Submilestone column repeats the Acceptance profiles table and M4's sequencing. In the Unverified native facts list, two facts (the nmstate-webhook Deployment name and MetalLB Degraded reporting transient failures) are still listed as unverified behind B755 and B757. M4 records those gates as accepted. Examples: `specs/add-on-coverage.md:42`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:48`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:11`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:416`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. Delete the six '(delivered)' markers and the 'Needs definition' text. For the two facts B755 and B757 met: if knowledge recorded them, delete them from the unverified list; otherwise name the open re-verifier. Drop the Submilestone column, and the Qualification column's gate ids, which Acceptance profiles already map. Keep the Item column, because the parity test and C3 rely on it, and update coverage_parity_test.go's coverageColumns in the same change. Keep lines 11-13 as a present-tense refusal ('naming a package the registry does not hold under spec.packages is refused as an unknown field'), without 'not yet delivered'.

<a id="add-p2"></a>**ADD-P2 Coverage table cells are paragraphs and restate the API page's fields and objects.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: API-94); source B.add-on-coverage; 8 instances counted. The Built-in packages table in specs/add-on-coverage.md:40-49 has 9 columns and 8 rows of 626 to 2,038 bytes. Six Native objects cells run longer than 400 characters: kubevirt 1,007, fdf 779, acm 652, gitops 629, metallb 571 and gitlab 521. The section is 24,564 bytes, 12 bytes under the 24,576-byte level-2 budget, so any added sentence fails the docs gate. The Typed configuration column restates per-package fields and defaults that api/addons.md owns. The column is not free prose, though. Examples: `specs/add-on-coverage.md:45`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:43`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:44`; `specs/api/addons.md:460`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend. Move each Native objects list from the table into its package leaf (### nmstate etc.) as a bullet list, kind and name first. This frees about 4.5 KB under the level-2 budget. Reduce Typed configuration to the bare member names and the timeout default the parity test reads, for example '`subscription`; `cephConsumerRef`; `defaultStorageClass`; `multiCloudGateway`; `timeout` (default `1h`)', plus a link to api/addons.md#package-&lt;name>. Drop the copied defaults and admission prose, which api/addons.md owns. Fix the fdf Provides / requires cell to 'provides `dataFoundation`; requires none' and keep the CephConsumer dependency in the leaf. Change the opening sentence (lines 3-5) so this page no longer claims to own 'typed configuration'. Make the edit in the same change as coverage_parity_test.go, and keep the operator-managed reason in the fdf row or point the test at the leaf.

<a id="add-p3"></a>**ADD-P3 The fdf section mixes an admission rule, vendor facts, history and speculation in unwrapped prose.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; new; source B.add-on-coverage; 8 instances counted. The ### fdf leaf (specs/add-on-coverage.md:185-212) mixes several kinds of text in one paragraph: catalog choice, an unverified native fact, pull-secret contents, a v1 incident, the TLS object gateway admission rule with its rationale, an install-route remark, a console-plugin exclusion and a list of candidate discriminators for a future specialization. The admission rule and the redhat-operators sentence are owned and stated again in specs/api/addons.md (Package fdf, lines 457-492). Examples: `specs/add-on-coverage.md:197`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:202`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:190`; `specs/add-on-coverage.md:209`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept, with this amendment. In the fdf leaf, replace lines 189-206 with one sentence that links the owner: 'fdf admits a TLS object gateway only under the trust rule of Package fdf.' Keep the pull-secret requirement (cp.icr.io, user cp, the entitlement key) as one sentence, since the operator must supply it. Move the v1 NooBaa observation and the candidate discriminators (lines 209-212) to .agents/knowledge/data-foundation-external-mode.md, or to B761's item text. Keep the redhat-operators uncertainty only in api/addons.md, worded once, with B761 as the re-verifier. Remove the release-range wording ('4.20 to 4.22') from api/addons.md as well, since R8 bars release ranges from a rule.

<a id="add-p4"></a>**ADD-P4 The same rule is stated in two to four places inside the page.** Medium; duplication; restatement; new; source B.add-ons. Two restatements on specs/add-ons.md are real. (a) The set of blocks a last package waits for is stated in full at 87-90 and again in the Requirements cell at 172. The two copies agree today. (b) The chain paragraph at 517-521 lists 'a collected plan, two plans for one CSV ... more than sixteen CSVs' as staying unknown. The next sentence (522-532) gives those same cases a reason and remedy of their own (planCollected, duplicatePlans, chainTooLong). Examples: `specs/add-ons.md:87`; `specs/add-ons.md:618`; `specs/add-ons.md:517`; `specs/add-ons.md:575`. **Rewrite and rule:** Amend, on specs/add-ons.md. Reduce row 172's last-package clause to 'and, for a last package, the blocks that section names'. Rewrite 517-521 so that it does not list the retention causes. Replace 'the remedy above' at 543-544 with an explicit anchor: 'the destroy-and-apply-again remedy of the observation rule (or, for an additive-apply instance, removing or correcting the object)'. The operator should not have to guess whether an unproved chain calls for a destroy. Leave the handoff-predicate links and the Secret-value sentences as they are.

<a id="add-p5"></a>**ADD-P5 Bounds, thresholds and diagnostics stated without a value, a name or a code.** Medium; untestable; ambiguity or vocabulary; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: REC-55); source B.add-ons. Four rules in specs/add-ons.md name a bound or a result by a word instead of a value or a constant. (1) 'A condition unchanged long after its object's other conditions is reported as stale' (412-413) gives no threshold. The code marks a condition stale when its lastTransitionTime is strictly older than the newest lastTransitionTime of the object's conditions, so 'long after' also misstates the code. Examples: `specs/add-ons.md:412`; `specs/add-ons.md:324-326`; `specs/add-ons.md:268`; `specs/add-ons.md:229`. **Rewrite and rule:** Accept, amended with the values the code already holds. On specs/add-ons.md:412-413, write: 'A condition whose lastTransitionTime is older than the newest lastTransitionTime among the object's conditions is reported `stale`; staleness never decides the check.' At 268-269, write 'less `clusterobjects.ClockSkew`'. At 229, name the request bound's constant, or link its owner in state-reconciliation. At 324-327, name the publication diagnostic's code and state that the refusal text follows the 256-byte bound of Readiness.

### 10.15 Architecture

<a id="arc-1"></a>

#### ARC-1 Controller run outcome after `prepared` contradicts controller.md and the code

High; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source A.architecture-2.

**Claim.** architecture.md (The adapter result protocol) says the controller runner reports `failed` only for a failure before `prepared` is published, and `unknown` after `prepared` and on cancellation. controller.md (The controller stage) says a run that failed after announcing its sources but before Go acknowledged the tools is `failed`, and `unknown` only once that acknowledgement may have been delivered. The code follows controller.md: it returns `failed` for a published but unauthorized run, cancellation included.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/architecture.md:1087`: "host-wide effect was yet permitted, and 'unknown' after 'prepared' and on"
- `specs/controller.md:803-805`: "announcing its sources but before Go acknowledged the tools installed nothing"
- `specs/architecture.md:1044-1045`: "is then 'unknown', and a controller run fails 'controller.unknown', its outcome"

**Impact.** An agent building from architecture.md would record `unknown` for a run that provably installed nothing, which forces a needless recovery. Changing the runner to match the spec would weaken a stated proof of no effect. The two pages disagree on the recovery path.

**Recommendation.** In specs/architecture.md (The adapter result protocol), cut the controller sentence at 1085-1087 down to a link: "The controller runner's outcome, `failed` or `unknown`, is set as the controller stage states." Make the same change at 1044-1045, replacing "its outcome still set by `prepared` as below" with that link. specs/controller.md stays the only owner. Its rule is that a run is `failed` until the tool-authorizing acknowledgement may have been delivered and `unknown` after that, cancellation included. That matches `protocolRun.unauthorized`.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: amend at High; third reader: stands.

<a id="arc-37"></a>

#### ARC-37 The `prepared` record is said to be apply-only, but destroy attempts publish removal preparations through it

High; contradiction; two pages disagree; new; source O.ARC-1.

**Claim.** architecture.md's protocol table limits the lifecycle `prepared` record to 'only on an apply's own attempt', and state-reconciliation.md:507-516 says a running attempt's preparation is 'the before-state its capability observed' and 'only an apply's own attempt may' publish it. The code also lets a destroy attempt publish a removal preparation. populateRemovalExecution sets PrepareRemoval only for Verb == Destroy, Resolution 0 and Attempt > 0. RunFor wires invocation.RemovalPreparation. The physical-erase capability passes RemovalPreparation: validate, and physical_erase_protocol.py uses PREPARING_PHASES. The Ceph host and other removal-power capabilities implement CarryRemovalPreparation. The spec depends on this: the erase receipt is 'durably recorded ... in the lifecycle attempt before shutdown acknowledgement', and the Ceph retained-root cleanup is retried from a durable receipt. No spec sentence names a removal preparation, how it is validated, or how a later removal attempt reads it. ApplyPreparations, at state-reconciliation.md:2625-2627, names only the owning apply's preparations.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/architecture.md:1002`: "once, after 'loaded', only on an apply's own attempt"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:515`: "acknowledged, and only an apply's own attempt may. A resolution observation"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2823-2824`: "It is durably recorded on the execution host and in the lifecycle attempt"
- `specs/ceph.md:1243-1244`: "absence before proving the Machine off. A retry with the durable receipt"

**Impact.** An agent who implements the runner or the record store from the protocol table would refuse a `prepared` record on a destroy attempt as a protocol breach. That breaks the erase receipt custody and the Ceph retained-root cleanup receipt, both on the destructive and recovery path: a retry could not tell a removal that already erased or cleaned from one that never started, and might boot another erase worker or repeat a guest cleanup. A reviewer reading the specs alone cannot check the removal-preparation code, because no rule states it.

**Recommendation.** In state-reconciliation.md#attempts-and-unknown-outcomes (507-516), say that a running attempt of an apply or of a destroy may publish one preparation: an apply's before-state, or a removal's receipt that its capability validates. Next to `ApplyPreparations` (2625), name the removal side: a capability that carries removal preparations receives the earlier preparations of the same removal's inverse (`RemovalPreparations`). Change the architecture.md:1002 bounds cell to 'once, after `loaded`, only on an attempt, never a resolution' and link the state-reconciliation rule rather than restating it. Name the test that holds a destroy attempt's preparation.

**Verification.** refuter: confirmed; judge: accept at High; third reader: stands.

<a id="def-1"></a>**DEF-1 Add-ons design opening says nothing is implemented and B90 'revives' it, but B90's first slice already shipped its definition digest and instance identity.** Medium; stale; stale reference; new; source A.deferred-a. The opening of specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md says nothing here is implemented except the step shape, yet in the same paragraph it says B90's first slice takes the normalized definition and instance identity from this page. B90's first slice is in-tree complete (X235). add-ons.md already owns the instance capability and the descriptor digest. The page therefore carries slice delivery state (C4/R8) and understates what is live. Evidence: `specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md:3-4` "B90 revives this design with a declarative"; `specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md:7-11` "B90's first slice takes only the normalized definition and the instance"; `specs/milestones/m4.md:1810-1811`. **Fix:** In specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md, replace lines 3-11 with an opening that names the live owners: the add-on lifecycle (add-ons.md, including the authored add-on's `descriptor` and its instance) and the add-on API for admission. Then say the sections below are design for later B90 work, and that only the step shape under Steps is admitted, without `fromInput`. Remove the 'first slice' wording, which m4.md#b90 owns.

### 10.17 Milestone pages, decisions and delivered records

Medium:

<a id="mil-1"></a>**MIL-1 The opening budget can be evaded: openings point to 20 to 30 KB decision leaves in Submilestones, which neither the read route nor any budget covers.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: COR-78, COR-68); source X11-milestone-system. The opening budget covers only the bytes before the first level-2 heading, and the M3 and M4 openings hand their open decisions to level-4 leaves inside Submilestones: m3a-open-decisions (16,294 bytes; M3a subtree 20,484) and m4a-open-decisions (24,057 bytes; M4a subtree 29,690). The gates exempt every page under specs/milestones/ from the section and leaf budgets, so these leaves exceed the 8,192-byte leaf budget with no exception. Only m1 to m4 have opening budgets; m7's opening (1,195 bytes) has none. The AGENTS.md read route ends with 'and what they link', which pulls in these leaves. Evidence: `AGENTS.md:8-9` "on the named milestone page read only the opening, the Planned slices row, the item's row and its '### B&lt;n>' ..."; `specs/milestones/m4.md:41-42` "Q61). **Open decisions:** Q26 to Q61 in M4a's open decisions, whose recommended baseline"; `test/docs/docs_test.go:24-25`. **Fix:** In specs/milestones.md's page-format bullet (lines 126-131), name the optional `## Submilestones` section, as COR-78 proposed. Require each submilestone's open decisions to sit in their own `#### <Mx> open decisions` leaf, and put a byte budget on each of those leaves in docsByteBudgets (test/docs/docs_test.go). Keep the general leaf budget off milestone pages, because that exemption is deliberate.

<a id="mil-2"></a>**MIL-2 Spec says the --sha256 prefix is exact lowercase; the media store and the X515 record accept other spellings.** Medium; contradiction; text and code differ; new; source M.delivered-11. cli/commands.md says a `--sha256` value takes only an exact lowercase `sha256:` prefix and says nothing about surrounding blanks. Since X515 the CLI uses the media store's NormalizeMediaDigest. That function trims blanks and lowercases the value before it strips the prefix, so `SHA256:` and blank-padded values are accepted. The X515 record states this loosening, but the owning CLI spec was not updated. api/machines.md:1116 states the same grammar for `spec.checksum` (blanks and hex case accepted) and is also silent on the prefix's case. Evidence: `specs/cli/commands.md:574` "prefixed by exact lowercase 'sha256:', and normalizes to lowercase hexadecimal."; `specs/milestones/delivered.md:16355-16356` "accepts the spellings the media store already accepted (surrounding blanks,"; `internal/managedos/media.go:115`. **Fix:** State the digest grammar once, in specs/api/machines.md (the `spec.checksum` row) or a managed-OS media section: surrounding blanks ignored, an optional `sha256:` prefix in any letter case, 64 hexadecimal digits in any case, normalized to lowercase. Name internal/managedos/media_test.go as the test that holds it. Replace commands.md:573-574 with a sentence saying `--sha256` follows that grammar, linked to it.

<a id="mil-3"></a>**MIL-3 In-progress items with no slice are missing from Active slices, and the check exempts them.** Medium; contradiction; delivery state or record shape; new; source M.m1-1, X11-milestone-system. M1 items B1562, B1563, B1566 and B1567 have Delivery `in progress` with no planned slice, so no Active slices row reflects the D276/audit 006 program. The docs check skips in-progress items whose slice is empty (`item.slice != ""`). B1566 is `Needs definition` while in progress, although only `Specified` is ready for implementation. M1's Next cell ('operator gates; X132's definition') does not mention the program. The rules allow a Delivery cell without a slice, so this is a gap in the rules rather than a literal violation. Agents still cannot see this running work. A guest whose profile declares data disks and that also holds a hand-attached disk fails the strict domain_disk_bindings ownership proof and reads unknown, not the added disk. The spec has no Not yet met paragraph naming B1119, although B1119 links this table. Evidence: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2415` "missing disks; a data disk attached by hand, also beside a profile that declares none |"; `specs/milestones/backlog.md:1666-1668` "requires the domain to hold exactly its frozen disks, so a guest whose profile declares data disks and that ...". **Fix:** In specs/state-reconciliation.md#observable-fields-by-implementation, narrow the Notes cell to 'missing disks; a data disk attached by hand beside a profile that declares none'. Below the table add one line: 'Not yet met: a guest whose profile declares data disks and also holds a disk attached by hand reads unknown; tracked as B1119.'

### 10.18 The corpus as an agent harness

Medium:

<a id="har-1"></a>**HAR-1 The index promises owning sections but routes 27 normative pages over 24 KB as whole pages.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: COR-26); source O.SUB-1, X1-index-routing. specs/index.md routes 43 of its links to whole pages, and 27 of them are normative pages above the 24,576-byte section budget, 2.38 MB in all: state-reconciliation 213,621 B, ceph 193,785, managed-os 189,546, substrates 159,472, cli/output 121,599, cli 117,104, architecture 113,776 and so on. The Sections table (index.md:39-46) names sections for only 6 of them (managed OS, state reconciliation, Ceph, CLI, contexts, substrates). Even for managed OS it lists 12 anchors and none for media store, root-disk discovery or host firewall. Evidence: `AGENTS.md:5` "- specs/index.md names the spec that owns each question. Load"; `specs/index.md:6` "the owning section below. A specified capability is not necessarily"; `specs/index.md:19`. **Fix:** Keep the defect but do not put the anchors in specs/index.md: it is held at 5952 bytes with 53 bytes free, and docs_test.go says never to raise a budget for growth that belongs in an on-demand page. Move the 'Sections of the largest domains' table to a new on-demand page (for example specs/index-sections.md), linked from one index row.

<a id="har-2"></a>**HAR-2 Most sampled sentences on ceph-coverage.md are qualification narrative, item ids and external facts, not rules a test can be derived from.** Medium; objectivity; stale reference; new; source X10-rule-form-census. specs/ceph-coverage.md, a normative page that index.md line 29 routes as release qualification, carries 116 B-id references (39 distinct ids) and uses open milestone items as the subjects of its rules in prose, for example 'B472 records the artifacts...' (line 23), 'B472's record names...' (111), 'B474/B79/B490 review input...' (171), and 'B472/B475 qualify each supported layout...' (387). That is delivery tracking written inside a requirements page, against C4/R8. Evidence: `specs/ceph-coverage.md:387-391` "allow multiple drive groups on one host. B472/B475 qualify each supported"; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:195-198` "The full virtual suite need not fit all services simultaneously on three"; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:3-5`. **Fix:** specs/ceph-coverage.md keeps only qualification rules that can be tested, written without item ids: profile naming, and what each matrix row records. Change the opening at lines 3-5 so the page owns 'Ceph provider qualification requirements' rather than 'M2' requirements. Move the item-to-coverage mapping (B472/B475 and the rest) to specs/milestones/m2.md.

<a id="har-3"></a>**HAR-3 Gaps and delivery state in rule text that no item tracks or that bypass the form.** Medium; stale; stale reference; new; source X3-not-yet-met. Several rule paragraphs carry delivery or owner-question state outside the Not yet met form: ceph.md:759 ('until B488's rehearsal reads them'), ceph.md:2793-2810 (a whole 'RGW multisite blocker' section stating B483 is blocked and 'remain open'), security.md:689-690 ('B78 retains real-hardware qualification' beside a link to a delivered record), state-reconciliation.md:2493 ('until it lands' plus a manual workaround), and 'pending the owner's Q60 under D173' at project.md:113, add-ons.md:622 and state-reconciliation.md:2451. Evidence: `specs/ceph.md:1108-1110` "has no forward or retirement exit today: only the orphan-acknowledged"; `specs/ceph.md:2795-2796` "B483's required native 'ceph rgw zone create' route cannot currently satisfy"; `specs/security.md:689-690`. **Fix:** specs/ceph.md:1100-1111: drop 'today' and 'until its item defines recovery'. Keep the present-tense rule that names the orphan-acknowledged deletion as the only exit without a covering erase policy, then add 'Not yet met: an interrupted physical deployment ... has no forward exit; tracked as [B659]' and a line for [B1084].

<a id="har-4"></a>**HAR-4 Rule sentences whose meaning lives only in decision text, including a superseded decision.** Medium; gap; decision log; new; source X4-history-leak. Several rule sentences carry a decision pointer (controller.md:112, security.md:81, managed-os.md:985, openshift-clusters.md:1106, security.md:964, ceph-coverage.md:429). Mostly the rule is already stated inline, so the pointer is redundant and the 'rule meaning lives only in decisions' claim is overstated. One pointer does not land in any spec section: managed-os.md:985 '(D153's settle rule)'. The finder's claim that an agent could build the superseded behavior is not supported. Evidence: `specs/controller.md:112-113` "D20's 'latest patch' is the latest at lock generation, and setup reads no"; `specs/security.md:81` "(D108 as D152 and D248 amend it); a"; `specs/managed-os.md:985`. **Fix:** As proposed. In controller.md:112-113 write 'each pinned component is the latest patch of its qualified minor at lock generation' in place of 'D10's and D20's "latest patch" is the latest at lock generation'. In security.md:80-81 drop the parenthetical '(D108 as D152 and D248 amend it)'; the bullet already states the rule inline.

<a id="har-5"></a>**HAR-5 Destructive and authorization sections have no index route.** Medium; gap; structure or routing; new; source T2-destroy-kubevirt-stop, T9-nvme-secure-erase, X1-index-routing. The index names 'mutation safety' in row 23 but routes the whole 213 KB state-reconciliation page. The Sections row for state reconciliation (index.md:41) lists only stages, attempts, continuation and removal, and state machine. It omits the H2 sections #mutation-safety (13,667 B), #physical-disk-safety (23,231 B), #confirmation-and-authorization (9,386 B), #selecting-apply-targets (1,757 B) and #comparing-desired-and-real-state (21,944 B). The Ceph Storage row (index.md:42) omits #devices-and-destructive-ownership (20,831 B). Evidence: `specs/index.md:23` "| Apply, destroy, continuation, ownership, mutation safety, GitOps readiness | state reconciliation |"; `specs/index.md:41` "| State reconciliation: stages, recovery, removal | stages"; `specs/index.md:42`. **Fix:** Add a row 'State reconciliation: destructive safety' linking #mutation-safety, #physical-disk-safety, #confirmation-and-authorization, #selecting-apply-targets and #comparing-desired-and-real-state, and add ceph.md#devices-and-destructive-ownership to the Storage row.

<a id="har-6"></a>**HAR-6 Three index anchors land on sections above the 24 KB budget with no subheading to narrow to.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; already tracked (B965); source X1-index-routing. Three index anchors land on sections above the 24,576 B budget. Row 42's #resources-readiness-and-access is a 45,203 B H2 with no subheading (ceph.md:1543-2180). Row 44's #storage-locking-and-publication is 44,214 B, with a 38,714 B leaf before its only H3 (contexts.md:234-833). Row 43's #resource-inspection-and-explicit-access is 37,749 B. Under it the narrow H3s #machine-ssh-sessions (9,181 B), #host-key-trust (4,634 B), #client-keyring-export (3,825 B) and #administrator-access-export (2,918 B) exist and the index does not use them; row 43 could be retargeted today without any split. Evidence: `specs/index.md:44` "| Contexts: layout, locking, restore, deletion | storage and locking"; `specs/contexts.md:234` "## Storage, locking and publication"; `specs/ceph.md:1543`. **Fix:** The ceph and contexts splits stay with B965; do not file them again. Keep one link to the parent H2 as well, because these four H3s cover about 20 KB of the 37.7 KB section;

<a id="har-7"></a>**HAR-7 Heavily linked de facto owner sections are not named by the index.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: COR-26); source X1-index-routing. Thirteen heavily linked sections are not named by any index anchor, although other pages link them as owners: substrates#kubevirt-machine-realization (36 links from 14 pages, 23,622 B), state-reconciliation#lifecycle-unit (34 from 12), controller#the-controller-stage (25 from 12), api#object-names (24 from 15), openshift-clusters#installation (24 from 11), state-reconciliation#produced-material-custody (23 from 13), ceph#frozen-release-and-trust (23 from 9), managed-os#automatic-root-disk-discovery (23 from 3), infrastructure-services#host-reservations (22 from 10), ceph-resources#cephconsumer (20 from 9), ... Evidence: `specs/index.md:45` "| Substrates: host, Machine, identity | host, Machine"; `specs/index.md:24` "| Managed services, host reservations, publication | infrastructure services |". **Fix:** Merge this into candidate 1. Its anchors become rows of the section-routing page, not additions to specs/index.md, which has 53 bytes free under its 5952-byte budget. A gate listing heavily linked anchors that no route names is optional and can come later; it should not block the routing change.

<a id="har-8"></a>**HAR-8 'Is this rule implemented?' is not answerable from the text: there is no back-link and no machine-readable gap register.** Medium; process; no check holds it; reported by audit 004 and still present (audit 004: COR-03, COR-05); source X3-not-yet-met. No test checks that an open item whose outcome is a spec rule has a Not yet met paragraph, that the paragraph sits in the owning section, or that the item still owns the gap; test/docs/docs_test.go checks only that each linked item exists, is not completed and is not awaiting acceptance. A rule with no paragraph therefore carries no machine-checked statement either way. This is by design: specs claim no availability and milestones own delivery, so absence of a paragraph is not a claim of implementation. The concrete completeness symptom is the ceph.md:1100-1110 text that names no item (see candidate 6). Evidence: `specs/index.md:51-55` "invariants in the present tense and claim no availability. An unmet rule has"; `.agents/skills/milestones-and-knowledge/SKILL.md:36` "never holds acceptance or baseline state; those belong on the milestone page."; `specs/milestones.md:3`. **Fix:** Make the one check that can be mechanized and leave the rest as procedure. (1) In the docs test that holds Not yet met paragraphs, add an ownership predicate: the linked item's section on its milestone or backlog page must link the anchor of the spec section that contains the paragraph. This fixes COR-05 mechanically, and the skill already requires items to link their owning spec section.

<a id="har-9"></a>**HAR-9 managed-os.md '## Installation' (87.6 KB) should become an Anaconda installation H2, a Network and registration H2 and a Physical installation H2.** Medium; structure; structure or routing; already tracked (B965); source X2-structure-budgets. managed-os.md '## Installation' (212-1527, 87,580 bytes) chains three subjects: the Anaconda request lifecycle (214-768, 36,144 bytes), post-install convergence (Network convergence 769-1008 at 16,630, FIPS 1009-1064 at 3,448, Registration 1065-1245 at 12,055; together 32,133) and five physical leaves (1246-1527, 19,286). Promoting them to three H2s is sound for findability, but the Anaconda H2 (about 36 KB) and the post-install H2 (about 32 KB) would each still exceed the 24,576-byte section budget, so the section exception cannot simply be removed: two new section exceptions or further cuts are needed. ## Appendix B. Working tables of the cross-cutting lanes

Each lane's own measurements and working table, as it returned them. Nobody verified these tables; only the
candidates a lane filed went through verification. They are kept because sections 2 to 6 cite their numbers,
and because the proposed splits, the routing traces and the list of unheld inventories are starting material
for the work that [section 7](#7-the-plan) proposes. Paths are relative to the audited tree.

### B.1 Index routing (lane X1-index-routing)

```text
Index: 79 links. 43 target whole pages; 29 of those are above 24 KB, totalling 4.25 MB; 27 of them are normative, totalling 2.38 MB. 33 links target subtrees; 3 of those are above 24 KB (45.2, 44.2 and 37.7 KB). The 'Sections' table covers 6 of the 27 large normative pages. 5 normative pages have no route (cluster-access, cluster-admin-credentials, managed-os-satellite, managed-os-subscription-source, ceph-subscription-dependencies). Of the 30 traces: 6 land on an owning section within budget; 2 land on an over-budget section; 17 reach the right page but no section (median load about 90 KB against owners of about 10 KB); 2 reach the owner only through a link inside a routed section; 3 end on an unrouted page or have a split owner (2 is both, so the counts sum to 30). ### B.13 Census of rule form (lane X10-rule-form-census)
```

```text
Sample: 240 sentences, 10 from each of the 24 largest normative pages by bytes (metrics.tsv, specs/milestones and specs/deferred left out; the 24th is api.md, 36,943 B; api/openshift-clusters.md is the 25th and was not sampled). Word counts are hand estimates (±10%); every judgement is a single pass by this lane. The tallies were computed with awk over the coded ledger.
- Mean length 28.2 words; 45/240 (19%) over 40 words; 12/240 (5%) over 60 words; the longest are about 170 and about 190 words (substrates.md 1567, 1599).
- States exactly one rule: 115/240 (48%); compound: 125 (52%); compound and over 40 words: 40.
- Names an actor: 166/240 (69%); no actor, passive or pronoun subject: 74 (31%).
- Names a trigger or condition: 98/240 (41%). Many invariants need none, so this is not a defect count.
- Names an observable outcome: 159/240 (66%). Refusal sentences: about 33, of which about 7 name a code inline and about 3 link a refusal table.
- Effect rules: 33; failure or unknown behavior stated in the sentence: 23 (70%), missing: 10. Of the 2 missing cases checked, managed-os.md 889 is resolved by the section's 'Failures and recovery' paragraph (899-906); substrates.md 1599 states only the name-collision refusal.
- Mixes in rationale or history: 53/240 (22%); 33 of these are also compound.
- Carries an id (D, B or X): 5/240 (2%), concentrated in ceph-coverage, controller (D257), api/environment (D153) and ceph-native-api (B483).
- Uses a vague word: 21/240 (9%), mostly 'bounded' without a bound, 'separate/independent', 'agree/consistent', 'currently' and 'may'.
- A test can be derived from the sentence alone: 91 (38%); with its section: 99 (41%); not at all: 50 (21%). The 50 are 10 cli/stops captions, 9 ceph-coverage sentences, about 11 owner-pointer or 'X owns Y' sentences, and the rest external facts and structure.
- Best pages for rule form (testable alone): api/environment 8/10, infrastructure-services 8/10, cli/output 7/10, api/machines 7/10, security 7/10. Worst: cli/stops 0 (table page; 47 sentences in 103 KB), ceph-coverage 0 (9/10 not testable), architecture 0, ceph-resources 0 (10/10 need their section).
```

```text
T1-nic-description: confidence 3, 54122 bytes loaded in 18 loads

T2-destroy-kubevirt-stop: confidence 2, 78600 bytes loaded in 17 loads
  - Which unreachable-host situation the task means. The spec gives no 'host cluster unreachable on destroy' rule, and three paths fail generically: the quiescence gate (destroy.in-use), the entry power proof (lifecycle.start-power) and the lend (runner.task-failed or kubevirt.lend-unproved). specs/state-reconciliation.md:2564-2567 only says a silent or unreadable target is unproved and refuses.
  - The code, Level, Certainty, Cause and Recovery of the new stop, and whether it belongs to the kubevirt package or the engine. specs/cli/stops.md:1-41 defines the vocabulary but no rule says when a case earns its own stop rather than reusing destroy.in-use. kubevirt.host-silent already exists with a different level and is raised only from evidence validators.
  - How the new code travels from the capability to the engine. The Quiescence type carries State, Reason, Stop and Remedy but no stop code (internal/reconciliation/lifecycle/contracts.go:373-390), and no spec describes this contract.
  - Whether a hosted Machine's new destroy can pass the entry power proof at all. specs/substrates.md:1626-1627 says a hosted Machine requiring the lend 'refuses new lifecycle work before registration'. The online-effect rule (state-reconciliation.md:2586-2597) removes it while the host runs.
  - Whether the abandon authorization applies to an unreachable KubeVirt host. specs/state-reconciliation.md:2024-2028 says only the provided-Machine enrollment offers abandonment, but the sentence 'every other step of the Machine runs as usual' leaves a hosted VirtualMachine's step unclear.
  - The meaning of 'cannot be reached' for the host that is a child's parent cluster. A host whose own Machines are stopped (the nested case) is expected to be unreachable until started. Whether the new stop must tell that case apart from a kubeconfig or network fault is not stated; the code reason text at capability.go:613 hints at it.

Whether `nvme-cli` ships is not stated. It is owed a knowledge page lookup, and the repo says Bootwright owns host packages, so this needs a product decision.
  - Receipt shape and deadline for a command with no host-written bytes or no host-visible progress: the 4-hour worker deadline and per-target written-plus-readback progress (specs/state-reconciliation.md:2895-2948) assume host I/O.
  - Whether a data disk with `onRemoval` of the new method counts as 'erased' for physical Ceph retirement exactly like the two existing methods (specs/ceph.md:1398 says 'either method').
  - Whether `erase=<machine>:metadataClear` relaxes an NVMe-erase target, and whether the existing 'only toward less' rule needs a rank (candidate 4).
  - Which qualification tier the new path needs: in-tree only, plus the owed B70 real-hardware rows? specs/milestones.md Completion and verification requires each destructive path to name its tier but does not choose it.
  - Whether the 896 GiB (`MaxLogicalOverwriteBytes`) and 64 TiB bounds apply to the new method. The spec calls them 'implementation bounds, not hardware sanitize capabilities' (specs/state-reconciliation.md:2769-2770).

T10-grant-expiry: confidence 3, 65100 bytes loaded in 18 loads
  - Expiry format, time zone and precision (date only, or an RFC 3339 instant): the policy page says nothing; the only precedent is the full RFC 3339 UTC stamp in specs/cli/output.md:1463. The task says 'expiry date', which is ambiguous between a day and an instant.
  - Whether the field must be a quoted string: specs/api/session-access-policy.md says nothing about string scalars, but internal/machine/sessionpolicy/decode.go:30 refuses any non-!!str scalar, and api.md:106-107 rejects timestamps only for environment input; an unquoted 2026-12-31 would be refused with the generic access.policy message.
  - Whether an already-past expiry is refused at install or accepted: specs/api/session-access-policy.md:6-8 lists 'document, subjects and targets' as validated and nothing else.
  - Whether an expired grant appears in `policy permissions` (specs/api/session-access-policy.md:112-114 describes only subject matching) and the grant-level JSON members, which no spec table or test holds (specs/cli/output.md:342 lists only `context`, `grants`).
  - Clock source and failure: no spec rule says which clock admission reads, whether once per batch, or what an unreadable or skewed clock does; fail-closed is assumed from specs/api/session-access-policy.md:105-107.
  - Whether expiry also ends a running delegated session: lines 109-110 say policy changes affect new admissions only; an expiry is not a change, so the answer is assumed to be 'no'.
  - Whether expiry binds the ordinary-entry route: lines 90-99 say the ordinary command runs 'with no grant', so it is assumed to be out of scope.
  - Whether the commit needs a `Contract:` line other than unchanged: the policy is stored as raw bytes, not a capability request, but the specs do not say so and I did not run the golden test.
  - Which test name belongs to the clock: no existing test shows the repository's injected-clock pattern for the sessionpolicy Service.

T11-controller-package: confidence 4, 66330 bytes loaded in 14 loads
  - Whether the new package is baseline or stage: the task says 'controller install', so I assumed baseline; the spec's split is in specs/controller.md:10-30.
  - Whether an existing receipt without the new package is 'complete' and whether a launch or the ready path must still pass (specs/controller.md:215, 382).
  - Which goldens and tests change: no spec lists them, so I found them with grep under internal/cli/testdata and internal/controller/prerequisites (specs/controller.md:247 names no code path).
  - Whether the setup state format (`bootwright.setup-state-v1`) must change: the spec says nothing for a changed baseline; the development policy says no migration, so I assumed it stays.
  - Whether the preview's core-package note list or the added-set bound need a change for one more package: assumed not.
  - Which package name the owner intends and whether it passes the requirement grammar and a supported dnf: not in any spec; the owner must name it.

T12-ambiguous-root-device: confidence 3, 52055 bytes loaded in 11 loads
  - Where a plan-time 'two disks' check would live. Plan has no BMC or disk inventory, and the specs place the uniqueness proof at apply before media insertion (specs/openshift-clusters.md:55-57). The specs never say a plan-time disk-count refusal exists or is wanted. I guessed the task means the existing stable-selector refusals plus the apply-time proof.
  - Whether hints beside a wwn or serial may widen the match. machines.md:869 says hints are 'narrowing hints only', but nothing says the agent's rootDeviceHints semantics with several hints (the installer's own matching) are conjunctive. The code passes every hint through (internal/containercluster/agentinstall/selection.go:438-449).
  - Which code owns the controller-side pre-insertion inventory proof, including the 'serial must be unique' rule. The specs name no package. I could not find it through routing and guessed internal/substrate/baremetal.
  - Which code and refusal identify the ambiguous-inventory case. specs/openshift-clusters.md:55-56 says it 'refuses before insertion' with no stop code, diagnostic path, reason or remedy, and it is not a refusal-table row.
  - Whether a serial-form selector can match two disks on the host. The agent receives only the serial hint (no size predicate, openshift-clusters.md:62), and the BMC uniqueness proof sees only BMC-listed drives. The text calls this the controller-to-installer race without saying so for duplicate serials.

```
